## What next

[Calibrate, activate, move](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/05-setup/first-moves/) is the first session with a connected gripper.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/05-setup/first-moves/ -->

# Calibrate, activate, move

Every session with the gripper starts the same way: clear what errors there are, calibrate, activate. Then it
moves. This page does it once with Motor GUI, with Python and over UART; [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
explains what happens inside.

!!! danger
    The jaws move over the whole stroke during calibration, and close with the set force afterwards. Nothing in
    reach of them, fingers included.

## 1. Power up

At power-up the gripper reports *Not calibrated* and does not move. Its motor must be calibrated too, which a
bought gripper is from the factory; a self-built gripper gets that during its assembly, [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/).

!!! success "Check"
    The gripper answers: Motor GUI's panel fills in, or a status poll returns a frame. If not:
    [The gripper does not answer](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/#the-gripper-does-not-answer).

## 2. Clear errors

The driver powers up in an error state until its motor is calibrated and it has run through its checks; an
E-stop, an over-temperature or a supply fault leave an error too. A gripper with an error does not move, and
does not calibrate either: clear first.

=== "Motor GUI"
    **Clear errors**, when the panel shows an error.

=== "Python"
    ```python
    gripper.Send_Clear_Error()
    ```

=== "UART"
    ```
    #Clear
    ```

An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; after an E-stop, send a command with the E-stop bit
at 0 before you clear. [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/) says what each needs.

!!! success "Check"
    No error is reported: Motor GUI shows none, and the temperature, timeout and E-stop bits of the answer are 0.

## 3. Calibrate

The gripper calibration finds the two end stops: the jaws open fully, then close fully, at low force
(500 mA) and low speed.

Each end is recognised when the jaws have stood still against it for a little over half a
second, and read under a light 100 mA push. Positions 0 and 255 lie just inside the two stops, so a full open or
close does not press on them.

It takes a few seconds; the result is not kept over a power cycle, so this runs at every power-up.

=== "Motor GUI"
    **Calibrate**, and confirm. When the jaws stop, the panel shows *Calibrated*; press nothing else until then.

=== "Python"
    ```python
    gripper.Send_gripper_calibrate()
    time.sleep(6)       # send nothing meanwhile; With Python waits for the calibrated bit instead
    ```

=== "UART"
    ```
    #Gripcal
    ```

If the jaws do not move at all, or move to one end and stop: the gripper is in an error state (clear it first, see
step 2), or the motor is not calibrated.

If the routine runs for 30 seconds and gives up, an end stop was not
found: something blocks the jaws short of the end, or the mechanism is too stiff for 500 mA.

If the jaws barely move, less than 1000 encoder ticks between the two ends, the routine ends without a
calibration: something jams them.

Until the gripper reports *Calibrated*, send nothing but status polls: a move command or a clear during the
calibration ends it. The gripper then keeps the calibration it had before, none after a power-up. Calibrate
again, and the routine starts from the beginning.

!!! success "Check"
    The jaws opened fully, then closed fully, and the gripper reports *Calibrated* (the calibrated bit is 1;
    `#Gripinfo` prints the end stops it found). If not: [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/#calibration).

## 4. Activate

A calibrated gripper carries out a move only while it is activated.

=== "Motor GUI"
    **Activate**. The panel shows *Activated*.

=== "Python"
    The activate bit is part of every move command, its fourth argument; send it as 1. To activate without
    moving, send a command with the action bit, the fifth argument, at 0:

    ```python
    gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(0, 30, 300, 1, 0, 0, 0)   # position, speed, current, activate = 1, action = 0, E-stop, release direction
    ```

=== "UART"
    `#Grippos` activates by itself; `#Gripact 1` activates without moving.

!!! success "Check"
    The gripper reports *Activated* and the jaws have not moved.

## 5. Move

A move is three numbers: the position (0 open, 255 closed), the speed (0 to 255: linear from 0.1 to 184 mm/s at
each jaw) and the current limit in mA, which is the grip force ([Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/)).
Start with speed 30, about 22 mm/s at each jaw, and 300 mA, about 16 N.

=== "Motor GUI"
    Set *Speed* 30 and *Current* 300 with their **Set** buttons, then **Close** and **Open**, or set a *Position*:
    the jaws follow, the plots show the position and the current, and the state says whether the jaws reached
    the position or stopped on something.

=== "Python"
    ```python
    gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(200, 30, 300, 1, 1, 0, 0)   # position, speed, current, activate, action, E-stop, release direction
    time.sleep(2)
    gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(20, 30, 300, 1, 1, 0, 0)
    ```

=== "UART"
    ```
    #Gripvel 30
    #Gripcur 300
    #Grippos 200
    #Grippos 20
    ```

Put an object between the jaws and close on it: the jaws stop on it and hold it with 300 mA, and the state reads
*object detected while closing*. Raise the current for a firmer grip, up to 1500 mA for a short grip, and the
speed once the motion is what you want.

!!! success "Check"
    The jaws reach each position and the state reads *at the position*; on an object they stop and the state
    reads *object detected while closing*. If not: [It does not move](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/#it-does-not-move).

## What the gripper reports

Every move command is answered with the gripper's state, which Motor GUI shows in its panel and the
library puts into attributes: the position, the current, whether it is calibrated and activated, whether a move
is in progress, the object-detection result, and the three error bits. [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
goes through them.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/ -->

# Operation

How a working gripper is used: what happens inside when it calibrates and moves, the interfaces it is driven
through, and what to do when it reports an error.

## In this chapter

- [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
- [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/)
- [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/uart/)
- [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/)
- [With ROS 2](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/ros2/)
- [On PAROL6 and PAR6](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/robots/)
- [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/)

The exact layout of every message and command is in the [API reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/ -->

# How the gripper works

The gripper is a state machine in the driver's firmware, fed by one command and answering with one status. This
page is what it does with them.

## The states

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> NotCalibrated: power-up
    NotCalibrated --> Calibrating: Send_gripper_calibrate / #Gripcal
    Calibrating --> Calibrated: both end stops found
    Calibrating --> NotCalibrated: not done in 30 s, a stroke under 1000 ticks, or a full command or a clear
    Calibrated --> Moving: command with activate = 1, action = 1
    Moving --> Holding: object found, or position reached
    Holding --> Moving: a different command
    Moving --> Idle: error, E-stop, clear, action = 0
    Holding --> Idle: error, E-stop, clear, action = 0
    Idle --> Moving: errors cleared, then a command with action = 1
```

**Not calibrated**

- After power-up the gripper does not know where its jaws are.
- It answers status requests and refuses moves.
- The gripper calibration is not kept over a power cycle.

**Calibrating**

- The jaws open at speed 40 and 500 mA until they have stood still against the end stop for a little over half a second.
- The push then eases to a light 100 mA for a quarter of a second, so the jaws settle against the stop, and the
  end is read there.
- Then they close the same way.
- Position 0 (open) is set 32 encoder ticks inside the open stop, and 255 (closed) 16 ticks from the closed stop.
  A move to 0 or 255 therefore ends in free travel and does not press on the stop.
- The two ends must lie at least 1000 encoder ticks apart. If they do not, something jams the jaws, and the
  gripper stays uncalibrated.
- If the whole routine has not found both end stops within 30 seconds of its start, it gives up and the
  gripper stays uncalibrated.
- While it runs, send only empty Send_gripper_data_pack frames, the status poll. A full gripper command,
  Send_Clear_Error or an error ends the calibration. The gripper keeps the calibration it had before; after a
  power-up that is none.
- A new Send_gripper_calibrate always starts the routine from the beginning, also after one that was cut short.
- The calibration pushes with its own current. The driver's current limit (`#Ilim`, parameter 16) stays as it
  was.
- Send_gripper_calibrate has no answer; the calibrated bit of the status turns 1 when the routine is done.

**Moving**

- A command with the activate and action bits set starts a move towards the position, at the speed.
- The move does not start at full speed: it picks up speed over its first 0.1 s. Over the last stretch before
  the target it slows down, so the jaws arrive at the slowest speed.
- The current is limited to the commanded value. This is the gripper's own limit: the driver's current limit
  (`#Ilim`, parameter 16) stays as it is.
- The driver runs its velocity loop towards the target and watches two things: the speed of the jaws and the
  motor current.

**Holding**: the move ends in one of two ways.

- **Position reached** (within 5 encoder ticks): the driver switches to position control and holds the jaws
  there. Object detection reads 3.
- On arrival the velocity loop's integral is dropped. While the jaws stay within a quarter of a position step of
  the target (about 9 encoder ticks), the driver does not push them: friction holds them, and a few mA are left
  after a move. Pushed further off, the position loop pulls them back.
- A new command for the position where the jaws already rest, within that quarter step, is reached at once.
- **Object in the way**: the jaws stand still before the target, pushing with nearly the commanded current, for
  50 ms. The driver keeps pushing with the limited current, which is the grip. Object detection reads 1 if the
  jaws were closing, 2 if they were opening.
- Either way, nothing moves until a different command arrives.

**Idle**

- An error, the E-stop bit, Send_Clear_Error, Send_Idle or `#Idle`, or a command with the action bit or the
  activate bit at 0 takes the gripper to idle.
- The motor is no longer driven and holds nothing beyond the mechanism's friction, so an object can slip.
- After an error, clear it; then the next command with the action bit set moves the gripper again.

## The command

Send_gripper_data_pack carries, in 5 bytes:

| Field | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Position | 0 to 255 | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed, linear over the stroke |
| Speed | 0 to 255 | 0.1 to 184 mm/s at each jaw, linear (40 to 80000 encoder ticks per second); see [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) |
| Current | mA | the current limit of the move, so the grip force; clamped by the firmware only at 2800 mA |
| Activate | bit | 1 activates the gripper; 0 deactivates it, and it stops |
| Action | bit | 1 carries out the move; 0 stores the command and leaves the gripper idle |
| E-stop | bit | 1 stops the gripper and raises the E-stop error, again at every cycle while the bit stays 1 |
| Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The same command sent twice does nothing new: the driver compares every command with the previous one, and only
a changed command resets the "at position" state and starts a move.

So a host may repeat the command at any
rate, which the CAN watchdog needs; to move the jaws from a held position to the same position again, change
the speed or the current by one.

An empty Send_gripper_data_pack, 0 bytes, changes nothing and is answered like a full one: it is the status poll,
and it costs the bus almost nothing. A host usually sends one full command per move and polls with empty ones.

Over UART, `#Grippos` is the same command: it sets the position, activates the gripper, sets the action bit and
starts the move, with the speed and current last set by `#Gripvel` and `#Gripcur` (20 and 200 mA after
power-up).

## The answer

Every Send_gripper_data_pack is answered with Respond_Gripper_data_pack, 4 bytes:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Position | where the jaws are, 0 to 255, rounded to the nearest step |
| Current | the motor current, mA; positive while opening, negative while closing |
| Activated | the activate flag |
| Action status | the action bit of the last command, as received; it stays 1 while the gripper holds, and the calibration does not change it |
| Object detection | 0 moving, 1 object found while closing, 2 object found while opening, 3 at the position |
| Temperature error | the motor's thermistor is above the limit |
| Timeout error | the driver's CAN watchdog ran out |
| E-stop error | the E-stop bit was received |
| Calibrated | the gripper calibration is done |

The answer to a full command is sent before the gripper acts on that command, so it still carries the state from
before it; the answers to the polls that follow show the move. To follow a move, use the object detection: the
action status only repeats the bit you sent.

The bits are listed in [Errors and status bits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/errors/), with the byte layout in the
[CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/).

## A grip, message by message

What a host sends and what comes back, from power-up to a held object:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as Host
    participant G as Gripper
    H->>G: Send_Clear_Error
    H->>G: Send_gripper_calibrate
    Note over G: the jaws open, pause, close: 0 and 255 are found
    loop only empty Send_gripper_data_pack frames, until calibrated
        H->>G: (0 bytes)
        G-->>H: answer: calibrated 0, at the end 1
    end
    H->>G: Send_gripper_data_pack(200, 30, 300, activate 1, action 1)
    G-->>H: answer: still the state from before the move
    loop every 20 ms, an empty Send_gripper_data_pack
        H->>G: (0 bytes)
        G-->>H: answer: position, current, state
    end
    G-->>H: answer: object found while closing (1), or at the position (3)
    Note over H: the grip is in, the next move waits for the program
```

## Object detection, exactly

While a move is in progress and the jaws are not yet at the target, the driver reads *moving* (0) as long as the
motor turns faster than 500 encoder ticks per second, about 1 mm/s at the jaws.

When it is slower than that and
the motor current is above 80 % of the commanded limit, something stops them. Once that has lasted 50 ms, the
state reads *object found*, 1 or 2 by the sign of the current. Below 80 % with the jaws slow, it still reads
*moving*: the object is soft and still being squeezed.

At the very start of a move the jaws are slow too. The 50 ms keep that from reading as an object, so a host
needs no pause before it trusts the state. Once the target is reached, 3, and it stays 3 until a different
command arrives.

The state is therefore a snapshot of each answer. A host that wants to know "did the grip succeed" sends the move,
then polls until the state is 1, 2 or 3, with a timeout of its own; the ROS 2 drivers and the PAROL6 software do
exactly that.

## What the current limit does

The current limit of a move is the gripper's Iq limit for the duration of the move and the hold. It bounds the
torque, so the force on an object, and it also bounds how fast the jaws accelerate: a low limit with a high speed
gives a gentle, slow-starting move.

The driver's own current limit (`#Ilim`, parameter 16) applies only when the driver runs as a motor. Gripper
moves and the gripper calibration leave it as it is, so a Send_Save_config or `#Save` stores the limit you set.

The temperature of the motor is the other bound: holding an object at a high
current for minutes heats the windings, and at 75 °C the thermistor stops the gripper.

## Timing

The driver runs its loops at 5 kHz; a move command takes effect at the next cycle, and the answer leaves within
a millisecond.

The CAN bus at 1 Mbit/s carries a command and its answer in well under half a millisecond, so a host
can run the gripper at several hundred commands per second; 50 Hz is a good rate for a controller that polls the
state.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/ -->

# Over CAN

CAN is the gripper's interface: the one cable carries it next to the power, and a robot's control board, a PC with
the CANvas adapter or any microcontroller with a CAN transceiver drives the gripper with it.

The gripper is a
Spectral Micro driver on the bus, so the frames are the driver's; this page is the part a gripper needs.

## The frame

CAN 2.0 data frames with 11-bit identifiers at 1 Mbit/s. The identifier carries the node, the command and the
error state:

![Bits 10 to 7 of the identifier are the node ID, bits 6 to 1 the command ID, bit 0 the error bit](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/can-id.svg){ width="600" }
![Bits 10 to 7 of the identifier are the node ID, bits 6 to 1 the command ID, bit 0 the error bit](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/can-id_dark.svg){ width="600" }

- **Node ID**, bits 10 to 7: which device. Every gripper ships as node 0; set another with Send_CAN_ID or `#CANID`
  and save it. Use 0 to 13: the driver's bootloader reserves 14 and 15, and a device on one of those cannot be
  updated over CAN.
- **Command ID**, bits 6 to 1: which message. The gripper command is 61, its answer 60, the calibration 62.
- **Error bit**, bit 0: in a frame from the gripper, 1 while any error is active. In a frame from the host it is
  ignored.

So the gripper command to node 0 travels on identifier `(0 << 7) | (61 << 1)` = 0x7A, and the answer comes back on
`(60 << 1) | error` = 0x78 or 0x79; to node 3 the command is 0x1FA and the answer 0x1F8. Multi-byte values are
big-endian; flags inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit.

## The messages a gripper needs

| Message | ID | What for |
|---|---|---|
| [Send_gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) | 61 | the move command: position, speed, current, the activate, action and E-stop bits; 0 bytes to poll |
| [Respond_Gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#respond_gripper_data_pack) | 60 | the answer: position, current, the state and error bits |
| [Send_gripper_calibrate](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) | 62 | the gripper calibration, after every power-up |
| [Send_Clear_Error](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) | 1 | clears the errors |
| [Send_ESTOP](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_estop), [Send_Idle](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) | 0, 12 | stop |
| [Send_Watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) | 15 | the gripper stops when the host stops talking |
| [Send_CAN_ID](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_can_id), [Send_Save_config](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) | 11, 13 | another node ID, saved |
| [Send_Respond_State_of_Errors](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors), [Send_Respond_Temperature](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) | 26, 23 | the driver's error flags, the motor temperature |

The [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/) has the bytes of each; the driver's other messages, which a
gripper does not need, are on the [Spectral Micro site](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/can/).

## A control loop

1. At power-up: Send_Clear_Error, then Send_gripper_calibrate; poll with empty Send_gripper_data_pack frames
   until the calibrated bit is 1 (a few seconds; the routine gives up after 30 s). Send nothing else meanwhile.
2. For each grip: one Send_gripper_data_pack with the position, speed and current and the activate and action
   bits set. Its answer still carries the state from before it; ignore it. Then poll with empty frames until
   the object-detection field reads 1, 2 or 3, or your own timeout passes.
3. Keep polling at a steady rate (50 Hz is plenty) if you set the watchdog: every frame resets it, and the gripper
   stops by itself when your program stops.

The answer to every frame tells the whole state, so a host never has to ask twice.

## Host checklist

- **Clear, then calibrate.** With an error active, the driver drops the calibration request; a clear sent during
  the calibration ends it.
- **During the calibration, only empty frames.** A full Send_gripper_data_pack ends the calibration as well, and
  the gripper keeps the calibration it had before (none after a power-up). Wait for the calibrated bit; the
  routine gives up after 30 s. A new Send_gripper_calibrate starts it from the beginning.
- **The first answer is old.** The answer to a full command is sent before the gripper acts on it. Ignore it.
  The polls after it can be trusted at once: an object is reported only after the jaws have stood still against
  it for 50 ms, so the slow start of a move does not read as one.
- **The action status repeats your bit.** It is the action bit you last sent and stays 1 while the gripper
  holds. Follow a move by its object detection.
- **An identical command does nothing.** To repeat a move to the position the gripper holds, change the speed
  or the current by one.
- **E-stop recovery:** first a command with the E-stop bit at 0 (and the action bit at 0), then
  Send_Clear_Error. While the last command carries the E-stop bit, a clear does not hold.
- **Watchdog:** with Send_Watchdog set, keep the polls coming. The gripper commands and the status requests
  reset it; Send_Clear_Error and Send_gripper_calibrate do not. After a timeout, fix the host, clear, and
  resume.
- **Current:** keep the commanded current at 1500 mA or less for a grip, and low for a long hold; the firmware
  clamps it only at 2800 mA ([Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/)). The commanded current
  is the gripper's own limit; the driver's current limit (parameter 16) stays as you set it.
- **Settings by number:** gripper mode, the thermistor and the gripper's measured stroke are parameters 92, 91
  and 93, read and written with Send_Get_Parameter and Send_Parameter
  ([Parameters a gripper uses](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#parameters-a-gripper-uses)).

## From a PC

The [CANvas adapter](https://source-robotics.com/products/canvas-usb-to-can-adapter) shows up as a serial port and
speaks slcan; `python-can` opens it with `bustype='slcan'`, and the [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/) wraps the messages.
Any CAN adapter that `python-can` supports works the same way.

## On a bus with other devices

A gripper on a robot shares the bus with the robot's joints or other grippers. Give each device its own node ID
(connect one at a time, Send_CAN_ID, Send_Save_config), terminate both ends of the bus
([CAN termination](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/04-installation/can-termination/)), and keep in mind that a lower node ID wins the bus
arbitration.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/uart/ -->

# Over UART

The driver inside the gripper has a serial port. It is not the gripper's everyday interface, which is CAN, but it
is the way to configure the driver of a self-built gripper and the quickest way to look at what the driver
reports when something is wrong.

## Reaching the port

The UART connector of the driver (JST SH, 4 pins, 3.3 V) is inside the body, under the coupler connector.

Unscrew the coupler connector, plug in the [USB-to-serial adapter](https://source-robotics.com/products/usb-to-serial-adapter) with
the UART cable, and open a terminal at 256000 baud with CR+LF line endings; the gripper's 24 V must be on for
anything but reading settings. [The serial terminal](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/05-setup/terminal/)
on the Spectral Micro site walks through the terminal setup.

!!! danger
    The port is 3.3 V. A 5 V adapter destroys the driver.

## The gripper commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `#Gripper 1` | gripper mode on (set and saved on every gripper); `#Gripper` prints it |
| `#Gripcal` | the gripper calibration |
| `#Gripvel 30` | the speed of the next moves, 0 to 255 |
| `#Gripcur 300` | the current limit of the next moves, mA |
| `#Grippos 200` | move to the position, 0 open to 255 closed; activates the gripper and starts the move |
| `#Gripact 1` | the activate flag without moving |
| `#Gripstop 1` | the E-stop bit |
| `#Gripinfo` | the gripper's state: calibrated, activated, the setpoints, the object detection, the end stops |

Only `#Grippos` starts a move. A session:

```
#Clear
#Gripcal
#Gripinfo
#Gripvel 30
#Gripcur 300
#Grippos 200
#Grippos 20
```

Wait until `#Gripinfo` reports the gripper calibrated before the first `#Grippos`: a `#Grippos` or a `#Clear`
during the calibration ends it. After `#Gripstop 1`, send `#Gripstop 0` before `#Clear`, or the E-stop error
comes straight back.

`#Estop` is the driver's E-stop over UART, as Send_ESTOP is over CAN. The motor is released, a running
calibration ends, and the E-stop error stays until `#Clear`. Motor GUI's **STOP** sends it over UART from version
0.7.0.

The [UART reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/) has these and the driver commands a gripper needs; the driver's
whole command set is on the [Spectral Micro site](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/uart/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/ -->

# With Python

The `Spectral-BLDC` library wraps the driver's CAN protocol, gripper messages included: one method per message,
and the gripper's answers unpacked into attributes. The ROS 2 driver and the legacy gripper GUI are built on it.

## Installing

In a virtual environment:

=== "Windows"
    ```
    py -m venv .venv
    .venv\Scripts\activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `COM` and a number (Device Manager, **Ports (COM & LPT)**): `channel='COM20'`.

=== "Linux"
    ```
    python3 -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER     # access to the serial port; log out and in again once
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `/dev/ttyACM0` (`ls /dev/ttyACM*` lists it): `channel='/dev/ttyACM0'`.

=== "macOS"
    ```
    python3 -m venv .venv
    source .venv/bin/activate
    pip install Spectral-BLDC
    ```
    The CANvas adapter is `/dev/cu.usbmodem` and a number (`ls /dev/cu.usbmodem*` lists it):
    `channel='/dev/cu.usbmodem1101'`, with your number.

!!! success "Check"
    `python -c "import Spectral_BLDC"` returns without an error message.

The source and the examples are in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python).

## The first program

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import time

# the adapter: a CANvas on COM20 (Windows), /dev/ttyACM0 (Linux) or /dev/cu.usbmodem... (macOS), 1 Mbit/s
bus = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM20', bitrate=1000000)
gripper = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=bus)

gripper.Send_Clear_Error()                      # clear first: with an error active, the calibration does not run
gripper.Send_gripper_calibrate()                # the jaws open fully, then close fully
for _ in range(150):                            # wait for the calibrated bit, up to 30 s
    time.sleep(0.2)
    gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack()            # only empty frames now: a move or a clear ends the calibration
    message, ids = bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.05)
    if message is not None:
        gripper.UnpackData(message, ids)
        if gripper.gripper_calibrated:
            break

for position in (200, 20, 200, 20):
    # position 0..255, speed 0..255, current mA, activate, action, E-stop, release direction
    gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(position, 30, 300, 1, 1, 0, 0)
    bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.05)      # its answer still carries the state from before the move
    time.sleep(0.1)                             # give the move time to start
    for _ in range(40):                         # poll the state for up to 2 s
        gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack()        # an empty frame: status only
        message, ids = bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.05)
        if message is not None:
            gripper.UnpackData(message, ids)
            print(gripper.gripper_position, gripper.gripper_current, gripper.gripper_object_detection)
            if gripper.gripper_object_detection in (1, 2, 3):   # object found, or at the position
                break
```

The answer to a move command is sent before the gripper acts on it, so it still carries the state from before:
after a finished move, object detection 3. The example reads that answer and drops it.

An object is reported only after the jaws have stood still against it for 50 ms, so the slow start of a move
does not read as one. The pause of 0.1 s is for firmware 109 and older, where the start of a move could briefly
read 1 or 2.

While the gripper calibration runs, send only empty frames: a full command or Send_Clear_Error ends the
calibration, and the gripper keeps the calibration it had before (none after a power-up).

`Send_gripper_data_pack` with all seven arguments sends the move; without arguments it sends the empty status
poll. `receive_can_messages` returns the raw `python-can` message and the node ID, command ID and error bit from
the identifier; `UnpackData` fills the gripper attributes:

| Attribute | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `gripper_position` | 0 open to 255 closed |
| `gripper_current` | the motor current in mA |
| `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status` | the activate flag; the action bit of the last command, which stays 1 while the gripper holds |
| `gripper_object_detection` | 0 moving, 1 object found while closing, 2 object found while opening, 3 at the position |
| `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error` | the three error bits |
| `gripper_calibrated` | the gripper calibration is done |

!!! note "Object detection in library 1.20 and older"
    Library 1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with its two bits swapped relative to the firmware:
    they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object found while opening) and 2 where it sends 1 (object found
    while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right. The example tests for "1 or 2", which
    is right with every version.

## Stopping

```python
gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(20, 30, 300, 1, 1, 1, 0)   # the E-stop bit: stops, raises the E-stop error
gripper.Send_gripper_data_pack(20, 30, 300, 1, 0, 0, 0)   # to recover: first the bit back at 0, action 0
gripper.Send_Clear_Error()                                 # then clear; while the bit is 1, the error comes back
gripper.Send_Watchdog(500)                                 # from now on the gripper stops 500 ms after the last frame
```

With the watchdog set, keep the status poll running at a steady rate; a program that crashes releases the grip
within the watchdog time.

## Several grippers

One `CanCommunication` per bus, one `SpectralCAN` per gripper with its node ID; every answer carries the node ID
in `ids.node_id`, so route it to the right object. The [teleoperation guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/guides/teleoperation/) couples
two grippers this way.

The complete map of calls to messages is in the [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/python/) reference.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/ros2/ -->

# With ROS 2

Two ROS 2 packages drive the gripper; both are built on the Python library and a `python-can` adapter.

## The SSG-48 package

[ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2](https://github.com/Lass6230/ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2), written
for this gripper by Lasse Stubbe Ebbesen, with example nodes. Its README has the installation, the topics and
the parameters.

## The MSG gripper's package

[msg_gripper_ros2](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/source_robotics_msg_gripper_ros2), a ROS 2 Humble driver
written for the MSG gripper by the UCLA Biomechatronics Lab and Ben Forbes. The SSG-48 speaks the same protocol,
so it works with it as well:

| Direction | Topic or action | Type |
|---|---|---|
| Command | `/gripper/command_joint_states` | `sensor_msgs/JointState`, the position in the gripper's own units, 0 to 255 |
| Feedback | `/gripper/feedback_joint_states` | `sensor_msgs/JointState`, the position in the same units and the effort in mA |
| Action | `/gripper_command` | `control_msgs/GripperCommand` |

Ubuntu 22.04 with ROS 2 Humble, Python 3.10 or newer, and a USB-to-CAN adapter that speaks slcan, such as the
CANvas:

```bash
pip install Spectral_BLDC python-can
cd ~/ros2_ws/src
git clone https://github.com/Source-Robotics/source_robotics_msg_gripper_ros2.git
cd ~/ros2_ws
colcon build --packages-select msg_gripper_ros2
source install/setup.bash
ros2 launch msg_gripper_ros2 msg_gripper_launch.py
```

The only setting that depends on your machine is the adapter's port, `channel` in `config/default.yaml`:
`/dev/ttyACM0` or `/dev/ttyUSB0` on Linux, `/dev/tty.usbmodem*` on macOS, `COM3` on Windows. On Linux, add
yourself to the `dialout` group to open the port without `sudo`.

## The description files

The gripper's standalone URDF and MJCF (MuJoCo) packages, with solid or fin-ray jaws, come from
[robot_descriptions](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/robot_descriptions); the product repository's
[ssg48_description](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/ssg48_description) guide links the
downloads and says how to open them. Its display launch file is for ROS 1; in ROS 2, load the URDF with a launch
file of your own.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/robots/ -->

# On PAROL6 and PAR6

The gripper is made for the Source Robotics arms. Both drive it over their own CAN bus; their software calibrates
it, moves it and reads its state, so a program for the robot does not talk CAN itself.

The tool centre point, the
mass, the centre of mass and the inertia for the robot's tool settings, on these robots or any other, are on
[Data for robot integration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/integration-data/).

## PAROL6

### Mounting and connecting

1. Fit `coupler_connector_PAROL6` to the gripper ([Mounting on a robot](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/04-installation/mounting/)). It
   carries a shaft coupler with an 8 mm bore and two M4 clamp screws for the joint 6 shaft, and the homing tab
   that joint 5 homes against: the tab goes on the same side as the gripper's cable connector, with an M3 × 12
   screw in the marked hole, as the last pages of the assembly manual show.
2. Slide the gripper onto the joint 6 shaft, orient it, and tighten the two clamp screws, one on each side, with
   blue threadlocker.
3. Connect the [PAROL6 gripper cable](https://source-robotics.com/products/gripper-cable) between the gripper and
   the M8 connector at the forearm. Only this cable: the PAR6 cable is wired differently and destroys the gripper
   ([The cable](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/04-installation/cable/)).
4. Keep the gripper's node ID at 0 and switch its termination on; it is the last node on the robot's bus.

### The joint 5 homing offset

Joint 5 homes against the tool, and the SSG-48's coupler sits differently from the pneumatic gripper holder that
the control board firmware's default offset (8900) is for.

Set `j5_homing_offset` to `8035` in `main.cpp` of the
control board firmware and upload it, as the PAROL6 documentation describes for the SSG-48. After the first
homing, check joint 5 with the pin through its witness marks, and master the robot if needed.

### Driving it

The gripper calibrates after every power-up and does not move before that. Clear the gripper's errors first, then
calibrate, then wait until the calibration is done, a few seconds: a gripper move or a clear sent while it runs
ends the calibration.

=== "Commander software"
    The **Gripper** tab: after homing the robot, press **Clear gripper error**, then **Calibrate gripper**, and
    wait until the status says calibrated. Then set the position, speed and current with the sliders and press
    **Move GoTo**. In RBTscript: `Gripper_cal()`, `Delay(6)`, then `Gripper(position, speed, current)`, with the
    current in mA.

=== "Python API"
    ```python
    import time

    rbt.select_tool("SSG-48")                              # the parol6 package; pinch fingers: variant_key="pinch"
    rbt.tool.calibrate()                                   # with the robot at rest
    time.sleep(6)                                          # the calibration takes a few seconds
    rbt.tool.set_position(0.8, speed=0.5, current=0.4)     # fractions; current 0.4 is 580 mA
    print(rbt.tool.status())
    ```

    The API allows the calibration 2 s before it sends the next gripper action, which can be too short when the
    jaws start far from the open end; the pause above waits for the calibration to finish.

The Python API's `current` is a fraction of the range 100 to 1300 mA: the gripper gets 100 + 1200 × `current` mA,
so 1.0 is 1300 mA, within the 1500 mA a grip may use.

Use a low value for a long hold
([Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/)). `position` and `speed` are fractions of the position
and speed bytes: 0.8 is position 204, 0.5 is speed 128.

The [PAROL6 documentation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/PAROL-docs/) covers the robot's side: the gripper
port, the commander software, the API and the tool centre point.

## PAR6

The PAR6 arm's control box runs the gripper on its CAN bus as a tool, with `coupler_connector_PAR6` and the PAR6
gripper cable (different from the PAROL6 one). The [PAR6 documentation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/par6/)
covers the tool configuration, the runtime's gripper commands and the firmware updates the box can do for the
gripper.

## UR5 and other robots

The repository has an adapter plate for the UR5 flange. Any controller with a CAN interface drives the gripper
directly: [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/) is the protocol, [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/) and [With ROS 2](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/ros2/) are two ready
implementations, and the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/) has every byte.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/ -->

# Errors and recovery

When the driver inside the gripper detects a fault it stops the motor, goes to idle and sets the error bit in
every CAN frame it sends. The grip is released: an idle motor holds nothing beyond the mechanism's friction.

## Seeing the error

- **The error bit** of every answer's identifier: 1 while any error is active.
- **Respond_Gripper_data_pack** carries the three gripper error bits: temperature, timeout, E-stop.
- **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors** returns every flag of the driver, which is where the other causes show.
- Motor GUI shows the errors in its gripper panel; `#Error` over UART prints them.

## The errors

| Error | Reported in | Cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|
| Temperature | the gripper's temperature bit | the thermistor in the windings reads more than 75 °C (`#Tlim`) | let the motor cool; hold with less current |
| Timeout | the gripper's timeout bit | the driver's CAN watchdog ran out: no valid frame within the time set by Send_Watchdog | the host stopped sending; fix the host, then clear |
| E-stop | the gripper's E-stop bit | a move command with the E-stop bit set, or `#Gripstop 1` | send a command with the bit at 0 (or `#Gripstop 0`), then clear: while the last command's bit is 1, a clear does not hold |
| Not calibrated (motor) | State_of_Errors, `#Error` | the driver's own motor calibration is missing: a self-built gripper before [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/), or after `#Default` | calibrate the motor |
| Vbus | State_of_Errors | the supply is below 9 V or above the driver's `#Vmax` limit, 29 V after `#Default` | the supply, the cable |
| Encoder | State_of_Errors | the driver's encoder does not see its magnet | the magnet on the motor shaft (a self-built gripper) |
| Driver | State_of_Errors | the driver stage's own protection tripped: overcurrent, overtemperature | lower the current; check the motor leads |
| Velocity | State_of_Errors | the motor exceeded the driver's speed limit | unlikely in a gripper; clear |
| Driver E-stop | State_of_Errors, `#Error` | Send_ESTOP was received, or `#Estop` over UART | clear |

A gripper that is not **gripper-calibrated** is not in error: it just refuses moves until Send_gripper_calibrate
has found the end stops.

## Clearing

Send_Clear_Error, **Clear** in the GUI or `#Clear` clears every flag, the gripper's E-stop included, and goes to
idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back: a hot motor, a supply that is still low.

The gripper's E-stop counts as such a cause while the E-stop bit of the last gripper command is 1: the driver
raises the error again at every cycle.

So after an E-stop, first send a gripper command with the E-stop bit at 0
and the action bit at 0 (or `#Gripstop 0` over UART), then clear. The next command with the action bit set moves
the gripper again.

After clearing, the gripper is idle and still calibrated and activated; the next move command moves it. A clear
sent while the gripper calibration runs ends the calibration, and the gripper keeps the calibration it had
before (none after a power-up).

## When the gripper does not answer

- No answer at all: the supply, the cable (and its pinout), the bus termination (about 60 Ω across CANH and CANL
  with everything unpowered), 1 Mbit/s on the adapter, the node ID.
- Answers but does not move: not calibrated, not activated, an error active, or the action bit at 0.
- Moves to one end during calibration and stops there: the other end stop is blocked, or the mechanism is too
  stiff for the calibration's 500 mA; after 30 seconds the routine gives up.

[Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/) goes through the symptoms one by one.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/07-maintenance/ -->

# Maintenance

The gripper needs little: every wearing part is printed, so a worn part is replaced by printing a new one, and
the mechanism is a rail, two racks and a pinion that want a little grease now and then.

Power the gripper off
before any work on it. Before you open the body, to reach the driver or its termination switch, unplug the
supply and touch earthed metal: static electricity damages the driver.

## Before each session

- The fingers sit tight on their jaw plates and nothing is cracked.
- The cable's M8 nut is tight, the cable has slack for the wrist's full motion and runs clear of the jaws.
- Nothing lies in the jaws' travel, and the gripper calibration finds both end stops.

## When the motion gets rough, and every few months of regular use

- **Grease.** A little lithium grease on the rail and on the rack and pinion. Remove the four screws that hold
  the linear rail to reach the mechanism, wipe off the old grease and the dust, grease, refit, and move the jaws
  over the whole stroke by hand before you power up. A grinding noise, a stiff motion or a calibration that
  stops short of an end are the signs that it is due.
- **Clean** the rail, the racks and the body, as in [Cleaning](#cleaning).
- **Screws**: the finger screws, the rail screws, the lid and the coupler connector; threadlocker where the
  assembly manual uses it.

## Cleaning

Clean the gripper switched off and unplugged. Wipe the body and the fingers with a dry or slightly damp cloth, or with a
little isopropyl alcohol on the cloth for grease; use no other solvents on the printed parts, and never spray or pour anything into the body, where the driver and the motor
are open to it.

The gripper is not waterproof or dustproof: keep it out of wet and dusty places, and blow chips
out of the rail rather than wash them out. Grease the rail again if the cleaning took its grease off.

## Replacing worn parts

The fingers, the jaw plates and every other printed part are in the product repository's
[Print files](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/Print%20files) folder;
the rail, the carriages and the screws are in the
[BOM](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/BOM). A replacement
finger is the same part as a new one, and the gripper calibration at the next power-up takes care of the end
stops.

A motor or a driver is not serviced but replaced: the motor by the GBM5208-75 of the BOM, after which the motor
calibration of [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/) is run again (the body has to be opened
as in the assembly manual); the driver by a new
[Spectral Micro](https://source-robotics.com/products/spectral-micro-bldc-controller), configured the same way.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/08-firmware/ -->

# Firmware

The gripper has no firmware of its own: it runs the Spectral Micro driver's firmware with gripper mode turned on. This
site describes the firmware release named in the version box on the landing page, for the gripper release the
site is versioned by; a new firmware release for the same gripper updates these pages in place.

## Which release does my gripper run?

Over CAN, Send_Respond_Device_Info returns the firmware version as its third byte; over UART, `#Info` prints
`Software version: <number>`. The [compatibility table](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/compatibility/) says which releases go with
which Python library and bootloader.

## Updating

A gripper whose driver runs firmware 104 or newer carries the driver's bootloader and updates over its CAN cable: the
host tells the driver to reset, the bootloader waits two seconds for a host, and the host streams the new image
into it.

Nothing is opened. The image is `spectral-bldc-firmware-V<number>.bin` from the driver's
[GitHub releases](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller/releases), with a manifest
`firmware.json` and the release notes.

| From | How |
|---|---|
| a PC with the CANvas adapter | [Motor GUI](https://motorgui.com/) over CAN: choose the release, the GUI fetches the image and flashes it |
| a PC, scripted | `host_tools/bl_flash.py` from the [bootloader repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/stm32f103c-bootloader), over CAN (slcan or gs_usb adapters) or over the driver's UART port |
| a PAR6 control box | the box updates every device on its bus, the gripper included, from its dashboard or `tools/flash_motor_firmware.py` |

The procedure, the bootloader's protocol and what to do when a flash is interrupted are in the Spectral Micro
documentation: [Updating through the bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/07-firmware/update/)
and [The bootloader](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/07-firmware/the-bootloader/).

!!! warning "Before you update"
    - Open the gripper or take the object out: it loses its grip during the update and until it is calibrated
      and commanded again.
    - An update may clear the driver's configuration (the release notes say so when it does). A bought gripper's
      configuration is in [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/), so it can be restored; note
      what `#Info` prints before you start.
    - Give the gripper a node ID from 0 to 13: the bootloader cannot address 14 or 15.

!!! success "Check"
    After the update, `#Info` prints the new release as `Software version: <number>` (Send_Respond_Device_Info
    over CAN), and the gripper calibrates. If its configuration was cleared, restore it:
    [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/).

## Grippers shipped before 2026

Grippers shipped with firmware 101 or older, which is every SSG-48 before the bootloader releases of 2026, have
no bootloader. Their driver is updated once with a programming adapter on its JTAG pads, inside the body under
the coupler connector, as described in
[Installing the bootloader on an older board](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/07-firmware/bootloader/).

From then on the gripper updates over CAN like any other. A gripper on firmware 101 or 104 works as this manual
describes, with the differences the [Spectral Micro site's version 101](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/101/)
documents: the calibration messages and a few commands.

## Release notes

The release notes of every Spectral release up to the one this site describes are in the appendix,
[Firmware release notes](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/firmware-release-notes/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/ -->

# Troubleshooting

By symptom. The error flags and what clears them are in [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/). The
faults in the firmware and the software that are known and not yet fixed, and what to do until they are, are
on [Known issues](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/known-issues/).

## The gripper does not answer

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| nothing at all | the 24 V on the cable; the cable's pinout (a wrong one has destroyed the driver already); the node ID the host uses; 1 Mbit/s on the adapter; the termination (about 60 Ω across CANH and CANL, unpowered) |
| answers, then stops answering | the watchdog ran out and the host did not notice; a loose M8 connector; a second device with the same node ID |
| the GUI shows *No connection* | the COM port of the CANvas adapter; another program holding the port; the CAN ID in the GUI |

## It does not move

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A([The gripper does not move]) --> B{Does it answer on CAN?}
    B -- no --> C[24 V on the cable, the pinout, the node ID,<br>1 Mbit/s, the termination]
    B -- yes --> D{Calibrated?}
    D -- no --> E[Run the gripper calibration;<br>a self-built gripper: the motor calibration first]
    D -- yes --> F{An error flag set?}
    F -- yes --> G[Clear it; if it comes back,<br>Errors and recovery names the cause]
    F -- no --> H{Activate and action bits at 1?}
    H -- no --> I[Send the command with activate = 1 and action = 1]
    H -- yes --> J[The command equals the previous one:<br>change the speed or the current by one]
```

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| calibrated, activated, no error, no motion | the action bit of the command is 0; the command is identical to the previous one (change the speed or the current by one to repeat a move) |
| *Not calibrated* after power-up | normal: run the gripper calibration |
| an error is shown | [Errors and recovery](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/): clear it, then look at the cause if it comes back |
| the driver reports *Not calibrated* in State_of_Errors and `#Error` | the motor itself is not calibrated (a self-built gripper): [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/) |

## Calibration

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| the jaws move to one end and stop; after 30 s the gripper is still not calibrated | the other end is blocked, or the mechanism is too stiff for the calibration's 500 mA: a tight rail, a pinion pressed too hard into the racks, debris in the racks |
| the jaws jitter and do not travel | a phase of the motor not connected (self-built), or the motor not calibrated |
| the routine ends within a few seconds, and the gripper is still not calibrated | the jaws travelled less than 1000 encoder ticks between the two ends: something jams them |
| 255 is not fully closed, or 0 not fully open | something stopped the jaws short of the end during calibration; calibrate again with the stroke free. By design 0 lies 32 encoder ticks inside the open stop and 255 16 ticks from the closed one (about 0.07 and 0.04 mm at each jaw), so that a full open or close does not press on the stop |

## The grip

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| the object slips | the current too low for the object; the finger faces: foam on the pinch jaws, or the fin-ray fingers |
| the object is crushed | the current too high; a hard object takes the full force at once |
| *object detected* while nothing is there | the current limit too low for the mechanism's friction at that speed; raise the current a little or lower the speed |
| the gripper stops with a temperature error after a while | a long hold at a high current; hold with the lowest current that keeps the object |
| the jaws creep or hum when holding | the position loop against a hard object; lower the current, or hold a soft object with a position slightly beyond the contact |
| the current takes a second or more to settle after a move; a full open or close keeps drawing the grip current and reports an object | firmware 109 or older: update to 110 ([Known issues](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/known-issues/), KI-11 and KI-12) |

## Noise and heat

A gimbal motor under field-oriented control is quiet; a grinding noise is the rack and pinion without grease, or
debris. The motor gets warm in use and hot under a long grip; the thermistor stops it at 75 °C. A self-built
gripper without a thermistor in the windings has no such protection.

## After a firmware update

The gripper calibration is kept in RAM only: calibrate after an update, as after every power-up. The driver's
settings and its motor calibration are kept from 109 to 110.

If the gripper does not calibrate or behaves oddly after an update, check the driver's configuration over UART:
`#Gripper` (gripper mode, 1), `#Term` (the thermistor, 1) and `#Info` (the motor calibration and parameters). A
release note says when an update clears the configuration; [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/) restores
it.

## Getting help

[Support](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/) says where to ask and what to include; the gripper's status and `#Info`'s output are
the first things.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/known-issues/ -->

# Known issues

The faults in the gripper's firmware and in the software that drives it that are known and not yet fixed, and
what to do until they are. The gripper has no firmware of its own: these are the Spectral Micro driver's, in
gripper mode. The pages that describe each part say the same where it matters; this page collects them in one
place. Which versions work together is in [Versions and compatibility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/compatibility/).

### Spectral driver firmware

Seen in: 110.

| | What happens | What to do | More |
|---|---|---|---|
| KI-1 | A gripper E-stop raises the E-stop error again at every control cycle for as long as the last gripper command carries the E-stop bit, so Send_Clear_Error (or `#Clear`) seems to do nothing. | Send a gripper command with the E-stop bit at 0 and the action bit at 0 (or `#Gripstop 0`), then clear. | [Errors and recovery, clearing](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/errors/#clearing) |
| KI-2 | The answer to a full Send_gripper_data_pack is sent before the gripper acts on the command, so it carries the state from before it. | Ignore that answer, and follow the move with empty frames. On firmware 109 and older, also give a move about 100 ms before you trust its object detection. | [Over CAN, host checklist](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/#host-checklist) |
| KI-4 | The action status in the gripper's answer is the action bit of the last command; the firmware never clears it, neither at the end of a move nor in the calibration. | Follow a move by its object detection and the position, not by the action status. | [The gripper's state byte](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/errors/#the-grippers-state-byte) |
| KI-6 | With braking in idle switched on (Send_Settings, parameter 18, or `#Brake 1`), the current that turning the motor drives through its shorted phases is not limited. Until firmware 110 the setting was not saved either (KI-14). | Leave the default, coasting, unless you need the brake, and do not force the jaws by hand while it brakes. | [Send_Idle](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) |

### PAROL6 Python API (parol6)

Seen in: 0.9.1.

| | What happens | What to do | More |
|---|---|---|---|
| KI-8 | In `rbt.tool.status()`, `engaged` is always true (it is read from the speed field, which the robot always reports as 1), and `part_detected` reads bits 3 and 2 of the gripper's state byte, the temperature and timeout errors, not the object detection in bits 5 and 4. | To know that a part is held, check the position the jaws stopped at, or use a sensor. | [On PAROL6 and PAR6, driving it](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/robots/#driving-it) |
| KI-9 | `rbt.tool.calibrate()` counts the calibration done after a fixed 2 s without reading the calibrated bit, and the SSG-48 takes about 3 s, longer when the jaws start far from the open end. The API has no action to clear a gripper error. | Wait for the calibration before the first move, as the example on the PAROL6 page does; clear an error in the commander's Gripper tab or with Motor GUI, then calibrate. | [On PAROL6 and PAR6, driving it](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/robots/#driving-it) |

### Fixed

| | What happened | Fixed in | More |
|---|---|---|---|
| KI-3 | A full gripper command or a clear sent during the gripper calibration ends it, and the gripper stays uncalibrated. The routine's counters are not reset, so the next calibration starts where the stopped one was (it can skip the opening) and counts the time already spent towards its 30 s limit. | 110: a new calibration starts from the beginning, with its whole 30 s; a command or a clear still ends a running one, and the gripper keeps the calibration it had before | [Over CAN, host checklist](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/#host-checklist) |
| KI-5 | The motor calibration (`#Cal`) sets the driver's current limit to 1600 mA and leaves it there, and `#Save` stores it. Gripper moves are not affected, they use each command's current; the driver's own modes, such as the current and position modes of the teleoperation guide, run with up to 1600 mA. | 109: calibration puts back the current limit that was in force when it started | [Driver setup and first run, current limit](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/#current-limit) |
| KI-7 | `gripper_object_detection` has its two bits swapped: the library reports 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object found while opening) and 2 where it sends 1 (object found while closing); 0 and 3 are right. | 1.21: `gripper_object_detection` reads the two bits the right way round | [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/) |
| KI-10 | A status poll (an empty Send_gripper_data_pack) or a repeat of the command that reaches the driver within one control cycle (about 0.2 ms) of a new move command cancels it as new. The move then runs in position mode, and object detection reads 3 while the jaws press on an object. | 109: only a new command marks itself new, so a poll or a repeat no longer cancels the move | [Over CAN, host checklist](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/#host-checklist) |
| KI-11 | After a move the current took a second or more to settle, and some of it stayed while the gripper held the position. The velocity loop carried the current of the move into the hold and unwound it slowly through the mechanism's friction. | 110: the integral is dropped on arrival, the last stretch is slower and the hold has a small dead zone; a few mA are left after a move | [How the gripper works, the states](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/#the-states) |
| KI-12 | The gripper calibration read the two ends while it pushed into the stops at 500 mA, so positions 0 and 255 lay inside the stops. A full open or close with less current stopped short, kept pressing on the stop with the grip current, and often reported an object (1 or 2) instead of 3; a gripper a few ticks short of 255 reported 254. | 110: each end is read under a light 100 mA push; 0 lies 32 encoder ticks inside the open stop, 255 16 ticks from the closed one; the position is rounded to the nearest step | [How the gripper works, the states](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/#the-states) |
| KI-13 | Gripper moves set the driver's current limit (`#Ilim`, parameter 16) to the current of each command, and the gripper calibration set it to 500 mA. A Send_Save_config or `#Save` then stored that as the driver's limit. | 110: the gripper and its calibration push with their own current; the driver's limit stays as set | [Driver setup and first run, current limit](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/#current-limit) |
| KI-14 | Brake or coast when idle (parameter 18) was not saved. After every power-up the driver coasted, whatever was set before Send_Save_config. | 110: Send_Save_config keeps it; a driver that never saved it coasts, as before | [System, parameters a gripper uses](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#parameters-a-gripper-uses) |
| KI-15 | With the watchdog's action set to hold or descend, a watchdog that ran out while the gripper was idle started the hold or the descend later, when the next gripper command arrived, for the whole fallback time. | 110: hold and descend start only when the watchdog runs out in gripper mode | [System, Send_Watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) |

## Something that is not here

Check [Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/) first. If it is still not explained, [Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/report-a-problem/)
says what to include so it can be reproduced. A fixed issue stays on this page, under "Fixed", with the version
that fixes it.

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/ -->

# Build guide

**The SSG-48 is open source, and that is important to us.** Everything the gripper is made of is published in the
[product repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper) under the CERN-OHL-S-2.0
licence: the STEP files, the printable parts of both hardware versions, the bill of materials with a link for every
item, the assembly manual and video, the fin-ray and pinch fingers, and the URDF and MJCF models. The driver's
firmware and the software that drives the gripper are open source too. A gripper you build is the same gripper as
the one from the shop, and this manual applies to it; design your own fingers on the jaw plate template, or a
coupler connector for a robot the gripper was not designed for. This guide is the order to do it in.

!!! warning
    A self-built gripper is yours to make safe: the thermistor in the windings, the current within what the motor
    stands, and the [Safety](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/02-safety/) chapter apply to it as to a bought one.

## The steps

1. [Bill of materials](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/bill-of-materials/): the repository's BOM, with the reference images.
2. [Printing the parts](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/printing/): PETG, the V2 set, the fingers in a flexible filament.
3. [Mechanical assembly](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/mechanical-assembly/): the manual, page by page, the video, the cable.
4. [Driver setup and first run](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/): the motor calibration and gripper mode during the assembly, then
   the first moves.

## Kits and the shop

You do not have to source everything yourself:

| | What is in it | You add |
|---|---|---|
| [Spectral Micro BLDC starter kit](https://source-robotics.com/products/spectral-micro-bldc-starter-kit) | the Spectral Micro driver, the CANvas USB-to-CAN adapter, the USB-to-serial adapter, an ST-Link with the programming adapter, the UART, power and CAN cables, the 6 × 2.5 mm encoder magnet, the 100K thermistor | the GBM5208-75 motor, the rail and its carriages, the shaft coupler, the M8 connector, the screws and inserts, the printed parts |
| [Spectral Micro driver](https://source-robotics.com/products/spectral-micro-bldc-controller) alone | the driver | the rest, and the adapters its setup needs |
| [Assembled SSG-48 gripper](https://source-robotics.com/products/compliant-gripper) | the gripper, built, calibrated and configured, in black or grey | the fingers, the [cable](https://source-robotics.com/products/gripper-cable), the shaft coupler for PAROL6 |

The starter kit is the good-value start for a build: it has the driver and everything the driver's setup needs,
the CAN adapter for Motor GUI, the serial adapter for the UART, the magnet, the thermistor and the two internal
cables, for little more than the driver alone. The [PAROL6 gripper cable](https://source-robotics.com/products/gripper-cable)
is in the shop too.

# Bill of materials

!!! note "This is a copy"
    The original is [BOM/README.md](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/blob/main/BOM/README.md) in the gripper's repository; this page is that file as of
    2026-11-05 (commit `599b987`), with the reference images shown inline. If a link is broken or a part is wrong,
    [open an issue](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/issues/new) there, and the fix lands here with the next sync. The shop's
    [starter kit](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/#kits-and-the-shop) covers the driver and everything its setup needs.

This BOM lists all components required to build the SSG48 gripper. Quantities are for **one gripper**.

!!! note
    If any product links are broken, unavailable, or no longer point to the correct item, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/issues/new), send us a message on Discord, or contact us via email. You can also use the reference images to find the same or an equivalent part from another supplier.

# Printing the parts

## Material and settings

PETG for the body, the lids, the jaw plates and the coupler connector; the fin-ray fingers in a flexible filament.
The assembly manual's reference prints were made on a Prusa MK2S in PETG with 25 % infill, supports only where a
part needs them: clean every support off before assembly, the bearing seats and the rail slot in particular.

![The body printed in black and in grey, the two colours the shop sells](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/SSG48_black_and_grey.webp){ width="600" }

## The files

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The body, the lid, the gear and the magnet shaft, in two hardware versions: print the `V2` set, the large-bearing version ([Hardware versions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/01-overview/hardware-versions/)) | [Print files](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/Print%20files) |
| The jaws and the guide cover (in the `V2` set), and the coupler connectors for PAROL6 and PAR6 (in `Couplers`) | the same folder |
| The fin-ray fingers and their jaw plate | [Print files/Jaws](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/Print%20files/Jaws) |
| The STEP files, for a coupler connector of your own (the generic template) or your own fingers on the jaw plate | [STEP files](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/tree/main/STEP%20files) |

The brass inserts go in with a soldering iron after printing, as the assembly manual shows for each part.
