<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/mechanical-assembly/ -->

# Mechanical assembly

The repository's assembly manual, page by page: the jaws, the gear and magnet on the motor, the motor into the
body, the connector and its wires, the driver and the thermistor, the calibration, the linear guide, the lid, the
coupler connector, the cable. Read it once before you start: some steps cannot be undone without taking the body
apart again. Static electricity damages the driver: touch earthed metal before you handle it, and hold it by the
edges.

<object data="../../assets/pdf/SSG48_assembly_manual.pdf#view=FitH&amp;navpanes=0" type="application/pdf" width="100%" height="820">
  <p>Your browser does not show PDFs inline: <a href="../../assets/pdf/SSG48_assembly_manual.pdf">download the assembly manual (PDF, 3 MB)</a>.</p>
</object>

[Download the assembly manual (PDF, 3 MB)](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/pdf/SSG48_assembly_manual.pdf)
[The assembly video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=127zXHKuqIg)

## The thermistor

The motor has a 100K NTC thermistor in its windings; the driver stops the gripper when it reads 75 °C. Put the
bead between the windings and fix it with a drop of thermal cement, which sets hard and conducts the heat:
thermal paste stays soft and lets the bead move, ordinary glue insulates it. Solder the leads to the driver's
TERM and 3V3 pads and keep them clear of the rotor. The thermistor and the cement are in the
[Bill of materials](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/bill-of-materials/#electronics), and the starter kit has the thermistor;
[Thermistor](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/04-mounting/thermistor/) on the
Spectral Micro site has photos of it on the board and in a gimbal motor.

## Calibrate on the way

The motor is calibrated during the assembly, not before it: once the motor and the driver are in the body, the
wires soldered and the thermistor in the windings, and before the linear guide with the jaws goes on (page 22
of the manual), connect the serial adapter and run [Driver setup and first run](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/). The racks would
block the calibration's turns, so the order matters.

## The cable

The gripper's cable is not in the box. [The cable](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/04-installation/cable/) has the parts, the wiring
diagrams for PAROL6 and PAR6, and the warning that the two are not interchangeable; the repository's
[cable guide](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/blob/main/Assembly%20manual/Building_cables.md)
is the original.

## The fingers

The fin-ray and pinch fingers, and fingers of your own on the jaw plate: [Jaws](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/04-installation/jaws/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/ -->

# Driver setup and first run

A gripper from the shop arrives with its driver configured: the motor calibrated, gripper mode on, the
thermistor on, everything saved.

A gripper you build has a bare Spectral Micro driver that is brought to the same
state once, over its UART port, **during the assembly**: after the motor and the driver are in the body, the wires
soldered and the thermistor in the windings, and before the linear guide with the jaws goes on (page 22 of the
[assembly manual](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/blob/main/Assembly%20manual/Gripper_assembly_manual.pdf)).

The motor calibration turns the motor several revolutions in both directions, which the racks could not follow.
This page is that procedure; the commands are the driver's, and the
[Spectral Micro documentation](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/) explains each in depth.

## What you need

- The gripper assembled up to that point, with the encoder magnet on the motor shaft and the driver mounted.
- The 100K NTC thermistor in the motor windings, held by thermal cement, its leads on the driver's TERM and 3V3
  pads. Both parts are in the [Bill of materials](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/bill-of-materials/#electronics);
  [Thermistor](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/04-mounting/thermistor/) on the
  Spectral Micro site shows how it is fitted. `#Term 1` below needs it: without it the driver reads below −20 °C
  and stops with a temperature error.
- A 3.3 V [USB-to-serial adapter](https://source-robotics.com/products/usb-to-serial-adapter) on the driver's
  UART connector, a terminal at 256000 baud with CR+LF line endings, and 24 V on the driver's power connector.
  [The serial terminal](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/05-setup/terminal/) on the
  Spectral Micro site shows the terminal setup; [Motor GUI](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/05-setup/motor-gui/) over UART does the same job in the
  browser.

## 1. The motor calibration

Restore the defaults first, so that nothing from another motor or junk in the EEPROM goes into the calibration,
then calibrate. The Spectral Micro measures the motor's resistance and inductance and finds its pole pairs by
itself; nothing is entered:

```
#Default
#Cal
```

The motor clicks, then turns, the driver prints each step and ends with `Calibration success!`. To stop it early,
send `#Estop`; `#Clear` then clears the E-stop before the next try.

The whole routine and its messages are in [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/05-setup/calibration/)
on the Spectral Micro site. `#Default` also resets the serial number the driver reports; note what `#SERNUM`
prints before you start if you need it.

!!! success "Check"
    The driver ends with `Calibration success!`. If it stops with an error, check the motor's three wires and the
    encoder magnet, and see [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/05-setup/calibration/).

## 2. The gripper settings

```
#Gripper 1
#Term 1
#Tlim 75
#CANID 0
#Save
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `#Gripper 1` | gripper mode: the driver runs the gripper state machine and answers the gripper messages |
| `#Term 1`, `#Tlim 75` | the thermistor on, the temperature limit at 75 °C. Without it the motor can burn out under a long grip |
| `#CANID 0` | the node ID on the robot's bus; 0 to 13, see [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/) |
| `#Save` | nothing above survives a power cycle until it is saved |

The current loop gains the calibration computes for the motor are what the shipped grippers use.

Motor GUI's
*SSG-48* preset, on its setup page over UART, writes this step for you: the current gains (firmware 107 and older:
`#Kpiq 7.0381`, `#Kiiq 4.2557`; from 109: `#Cbw 300`, `#Kpiq 4.9018`, `#Kiiq 2.6993` and tool id 1), gripper
mode, the thermistor and the CAN ID (6, the PAR6 gripper's; change it before applying for another robot), then
saves.

!!! success "Check"
    After a power cycle, `#Gripper` and `#Term` print 1, `#Tlim` 75 and `#CANID` the node ID; `#Temp` prints the
    room temperature, not `Temp Off`. A temperature error at once means the thermistor is not connected
    ([The thermistor](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/mechanical-assembly/#the-thermistor)).

## 3. Finish the assembly and calibrate the gripper

Fit the linear guide with the jaws, the lid and the coupler connector, power the gripper up through its cable,
and run the gripper calibration (`#Gripcal`, or Motor GUI's **Calibrate**): the jaws open fully and close fully.

Then a first move at a low current, as in [Calibrate, activate, move](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/05-setup/first-moves/). `#Gripinfo` prints the
gripper's state, including the end stops the calibration found.

!!! success "Check"
    The jaws open fully and close fully, the gripper reports *Calibrated*, and the first moves reach their
    positions. If the calibration gives up after 30 s: [Calibration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/#calibration).

## Current limit

The gripper's moves use the current limit of each command, not the driver's `#Ilim`, and they leave `#Ilim` as
it is: a `#Save` after gripper moves stores the limit you set. The firmware clamps the command's current only
at 2800 mA; [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) says what is safe for the motor.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/performance/ -->

# Performance tests

Thermal tests of the SSG-48 gripper under different conditions. The thermal limit is 75 °C at the thermistor in
the motor windings.

!!! warning
    A gripper built without a thermistor in the windings has no temperature protection and can damage its motor
    in normal operation.

## Several days of cycling

- Open and close every 2.5 s, no load: the current near 0
- 7 days without interruption
- Motor temperature: 42 °C
- Ambient temperature: 33 °C

## Holding at a constant current

- Hold an object at 300 mA for 24 hours
- Stable motor temperature: 62 °C
- Ambient temperature: 33 °C

## The current that trips the thermal limit

- Hold an object at 1600 mA
- The temperature error trips after 4 minutes
- Ambient temperature: 33 °C

What this means for use: a hold at 300 mA (about 16 N) ran 24 hours without reaching the limit; a grip at 1500 mA
(about 80 N, ideal) is for seconds, not minutes. Between the two, the motor heats in proportion to the square of the current.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/firmware-release-notes/ -->

# Firmware release notes

What changed in each release of the Spectral firmware the gripper runs, from the release notes in the driver's
repository, up to the release this site describes. Entries about the driver's motion modes do not concern a
gripper; the gripper mode, the CAN protocol and the bootloader do.

## V110 (2026-11-13)

Spectral BLDC firmware **V110** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader. Mostly gripper work: an SSG-48 gripper (a Spectral Micro in gripper mode) now ends its moves cleanly and closes fully at position 255. Everything below is described in the manual: [Spectral Micro docs](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/); what a driver keeps and what to run after the update: [Upgrading from older firmware](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/07-firmware/upgrading/).

#### Grippers
- **A move ends cleanly.** On 109 the current took over two seconds to settle after a move: the speed loop's integral was carried into the hold and unwound slowly through friction. Now the integral is dropped on arrival, the last stretch of a move slows down, and the hold has a small dead zone (a quarter of a position count). A few mA are left after a move.
- **A soft start.** A move picks up speed over 0.1 s instead of starting at full speed.
- **Positions 0 and 255 clear the stops, and 255 is fully closed.** On 109 the calibration read the ends while pushing at 500 mA, so 0 and 255 lay inside the stops: a full open or close pressed on the stop, drew the grip current for good and often reported an object. Each end is now read under a light 100 mA push (released to no current, the SSG-48's free-running jaws spring back about 1 mm off the stop); 0 sits 32 ticks inside the open stop and 255 16 ticks from the closed one. On an SSG-48 the jaws stop 0.12 mm short of fully closed at 255, and the calibration repeats within 4 ticks.
- **Object detection** reports an object after the jaws have stood still against it for 50 ms.
- **The gripper pushes with its own current limit.** On 109 every gripper command overwrote the driver's current limit (parameter 16) with its grip current, and a Save config then stored it.
- The gripper calibration can be started again while it runs, ends on a timeout or a stroke under 1000 ticks, and puts the current limit back. The position is rounded to the nearest count (it was cut off).

#### CAN bus
- **Parameters 90-93:** 90 `#Rstint`, 91 the thermistor (`#Term`), 92 gripper mode (`#Gripper`, written only while idle), each 0 or 1 and saved by Save config, so a preset over CAN can set everything (issue #1); 93, read only, the gripper's stroke between positions 0 and 255 in ticks (0 until calibrated).

#### UART
- **`#Estop`:** the E-stop, as CAN has it. The motor is released, a running calibration ends, and the E-stop latches until `#Clear`.
- **`#Close` during a motor calibration** stops the calibration (`Close: the calibration is stopped`). On 109 it switched the mode under the running calibration.

#### Settings and safety
- **Brake or coast when idle (parameter 18) is saved** by Save config. On 109 it was back to its default at every power-up. A driver that never saved it coasts, as before.
- **Watchdog:** a trip while the driver is idle no longer starts the hold or the descend (on 109 it did, for the whole fallback time). A trip while a loop is closed holds as before.

#### Compatibility
- The settings and the motor calibration of 109 are kept. The gripper calibration is kept in RAM, as always: calibrate the gripper after the update.
- Python library **1.22** (`pip install --upgrade Spectral-BLDC`) names parameters 90-93; 1.21 reads them by number. Motor GUI **0.7.0** uses what 110 adds: STOP over UART sends `#Estop`, brake or coast counts as saved, a preset over CAN writes 90-92.
- Bench-tested for this release on an SSG-48 gripper: the moves and the hold, moves of one count, the ends and the closed gap, the soft start, gripping objects, the calibration's repeatability, parameters 90-93, brake or coast over a save and a restart, the driver's current limit through gripper moves, the watchdog while idle and in a closed loop, an aborted gripper calibration. `#Estop` and `#Close` were tried over UART on the STEPFOC, which has the same code. Not tested on the bench: an upgrade from V103 with the ST-Link, and a downgrade.

#### Assets
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V110.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `eae54f56b4d0eb3677155447a5ce68156bfbda16e81534513ad71cb0dbbbfb21`
- Size: 112984 bytes

Built from commit 38d210d on `Bootloader_main` (`#Info` shows it as `Build: 38D210D`). Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V109 (2026-11-10)

Spectral Micro BLDC firmware **V109** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader. From 109 the Spectral Micro and the STEPFOC share their version numbers, so there is no 108: 109 follows 107. Everything below is described in the manual: [Spectral Micro docs](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/); what a driver keeps and what to run after the update: [Upgrading from older firmware](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/07-firmware/upgrading/).

#### Phase B (the main fix)
- In every release up to 107 the gate driver's phase-B enable input was fed by the microcontroller's 8 MHz clock output instead of a steady level, so phase B could drop out: weaker or uneven torque, a calibration that failed with a wrong pole-pair count, or a motor that took a current command and did not move, with no error. 109 drives the pin properly. On the bench: 5 of 5 calibrations and full torque on every test, also over 10 restarts.
- The calibration now reports the true phase resistance and inductance (on the reference gimbal motor about 7.0-7.2 Ω and 1.75-1.9 mH, where 107 reported about 6.4 Ω and 1.25 mH); the old × 1.25 correction is gone.
- **After the update:** a calibration made with 107 keeps working. Calibrate again (`#Cal`) where the motor can turn freely, so the current gains follow the true values. An assembled SSG-48 gripper keeps its calibration: apply Motor GUI's SSG-48 preset instead, with the gripper's CAN ID set first.

#### New features
- **Parameters:** any setting or read-out by number over CAN (commands 36-38) or `#Par` (parameters 1-89). Identity (39) and telemetry (40) frames.
- **Capture, histogram and buffers** (41-43).
- **Watchdog actions:** idle, brake, coast, hold the position, or descend at a capped speed, with a fallback time.
- **Current loop from R, L and one bandwidth** (parameter 49, default 160 Hz; the SSG-48 preset uses 300 Hz). Measured on the bench and on by default: the direct PLL speed estimate at 100 Hz and commutation delay compensation of 234 µs (a speed step overshoots about 18 % instead of 63 %).
- **Encoder table and anti-cogging measured on the driver:** `#Cal` runs the calibration, then both, and saves; `#Calonly` is the calibration alone.
- **Sound through the motor:** tones, a queue of notes and samples (CAN 44 and 45, `#Tone`).
- **Identification:** `#Info` and parameters 84-87 report the build (git commit), the board ID and a calibration ID. Parameters 88 and 89 are an experimental current-sampling diagnostic, off by default.
- **Settings in blocks with their own checksums;** a reset keeps the CAN ID; a product lock refuses a STEPFOC image on a Spectral board.

#### Calibration
- Both current sensors are averaged; pole pairs 1-49; a rotor that does not follow the open-loop field ends with `Open loop: Failed` and two hint lines; an inductance that gives no gains fails the calibration instead of hanging.
- Kt and KV are measured in four spins alternating direction; a warning only when two same-direction spins differ by more than 5 %.
- The gate driver stays awake for the whole calibration. A failed calibration switches the bridge off at once and enables all three phases again. An E-stop ends a calibration, and `#Cal` is refused while one is latched. Calibrating many times without a power cycle no longer uses up memory.

#### Safety
- The control loop keeps the gate driver awake in every driving mode: a command arriving at the wrong moment could leave it asleep, with no torque and no error, until the next idle.
- Limits: a negative or not-a-number value is ignored by the legacy CAN frames (limits, gains, Kt, voltage limit 0-60000 mV); `#Ilim` and `#Vlimit` take the magnitude; the current of a gripper move stays within 0-2800 mA; `#PP` and parameter 78 take 1-49 pole pairs, only while idle (50 and more would read as a STEPFOC calibration at the next start). PWM duties stay between 0 and 100 %.
- The current-sense zero waits for the motor supply: started on USB before the supply, the driver used a zero about 100 mA off. It now says so in `#Info` and measures the zero by itself once the supply is there.
- `#Error` says `FAULT pin is LOW: the gate driver reports a fault` (the text said HIGH). No undervoltage error while the supply ramps up at power-up.

#### CAN bus
- A gripper poll right after a new move command no longer cancels it as new: object detection reports contact again (it read "at position" while pressing on an object). The same in every release before 109.
- The current and PD frames set their setpoint and mode together. Length codes above 8 are read as 8; extended (29-bit) frames are ignored.
- Watchdog: setting its time or a save starts a fresh window; a negative time means off; hold and descend no longer use the last moving loop's delay compensation.

#### Bug fixes
- After `#Cal`, a host that takes the driver within 3 s drops the encoder-table and anti-cogging runs. `#Encal` and `#Cogcal` start only on their own words. While such a run turns the motor, a capture is not armed and the histogram is not changed.
- A storage block whose check fails is read up to three times before its defaults are used. `#Info` says the anti-cogging is saved only while what is in RAM equals what is stored.
- The sound queue and sample buffer no longer replay old content after a stop; a pitch the driver cannot play answers `Tone: not played`.

#### Compatibility
- Python library **1.21 or newer** (`pip install --upgrade Spectral-BLDC`), Motor GUI **0.5.0**.
- Bench-tested for this release: calibration, current mode, restarts, the E-stop, the encoder table and anti-cogging, and the SSG-48 gripper on its 107 calibration. Not tested on the bench: an upgrade from V103 with the ST-Link, a downgrade, and on the Spectral Micro the watchdog actions, the capture and the sound (the same code passed on the STEPFOC).

#### Assets
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V109.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `96945eec70be12f0e74c6add5fd9fafd4054677e4ebf29d0380062c77a4f6d87`
- Size: 112420 bytes

Built from commit b5cedd5 on `Bootloader_main` (`#Info` shows it as `Build: B5CEDD5`). Includes bootloader entry support (CAN/UART reset-into-bootloader).

## V107 (2026-08-26)

Spectral BLDC firmware **V107** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

#### CAN bus
- Fixed `IN_DATA_PACK_PD` writing the commanded speed into `Feedforward_speed` instead of `Velocity_setpoint` — PD mode's KD (velocity-damping) term was being evaluated against a stale/zero setpoint, so it silently ignored the commanded speed.
- Added a generic mask+value settings command (`IN_SETTINGS`) for CAN-unreachable boolean settings, starting with idle-mode brake/coast selection.

#### Usability
- Idle mode can now be set to brake (driver stays enabled, phases held shorted via a zero-voltage PWM vector) or coast (Hi-Z, previous/default behavior), via `IN_SETTINGS` over CAN or `#Brake <0|1>` over UART.

#### Calibration
- Fixed `#Cal` spuriously failing with "Commutation/alignment check failed!" on some individual motor units. The pre-check that confirms the motor responds to a current command was driving a fixed voltage at the raw (uncalibrated) encoder angle; whether that produced torque depended on each unit's random magnet-to-encoder mounting angle. It now retries once at a 90-degree angle bias before failing.

#### Assets
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V107.bin` — application firmware image (flash at `0x08003000`, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `2ca1f2e3ad3ee7848cf47d8733b084be2daa87fc2e49f954dd41c76405d48ada`
- Size: 95404 bytes

Built from commit `2e7febc` on `Bootloader_main`.

## V106 (2026-07-06)

Spectral BLDC firmware **V106** — application image for flashing via the Spectral bootloader.

**CAN bus**
- The controller now drains up to 8 CAN messages per pass instead of just 1, so short bursts (multiple commands sent back-to-back, or a busy multi-node bus) no longer silently drop messages once the 3-deep hardware FIFO fills.
- A CAN peripheral that fails to initialize no longer bricks the board — UART stays fully usable, only the CAN bus is skipped.

**Safety**
- Added a hardware watchdog (100ms). If the control loop ever stops running, the board resets instead of leaving the motor driven at a stale duty cycle.
- Fixed a bug where `Torque_mode` could silently overwrite your commanded Iq setpoint when clamping to the current limit — reading it back after clamping now shows what you actually asked for, and raising the current limit afterward immediately restores the original commanded torque instead of requiring the command to be resent.
- Fixed undefined behavior in a serial-protocol integer conversion (`fourBytesToInt`).
- Synced default configuration values that had drifted between two locations in the code, so a fresh `#Default` and a freshly-flashed board's built-in defaults now agree.

**EEPROM / configuration integrity**
- Added CRC validation over the saved configuration, split into two independent halves: calibration data (resistance, inductance, Kt/KV, angle offset, current-loop gains, etc.) and settings (PID tuning, limits, watchdog config, CAN ID, etc.).
- This means a corrupted save (e.g. from a power loss mid-write) is detected and safely defaulted instead of silently running with garbage values — and critically, a future firmware update that only adds a new setting can no longer wipe your calibration, since the two are validated independently.
- Boards upgrading from older, pre-CRC firmware keep their existing calibration automatically — no need to recalibrate after this update.
- A few unused slots were reserved in the calibration block for upcoming features (e.g. magnet alignment), so those can be added later without another migration.

**Performance**
- PWM output no longer re-resolves which timer/channel it's writing to on every single call (it was doing this 4x per control tick) — resolved once and cached, freeing up ISR headroom.
- Velocity calculation switched from a floating-point divide to an integer multiply.

**Usability**
- New `#Help` command — prints a summary of the available commands.
- Serial now responds with `"Unknown command"` for unrecognized input instead of silently ignoring it.
- Calibration now prints progress during the angle-offset search (previously up to ~40 seconds of silence that could look like the board had hung).
- `#Info` now always reports live ISR execution time, useful for checking control-loop headroom on the bench.
- Fixed a leftover calibration-failure message that incorrectly suggested swapping motor phases — that failure mode no longer exists (reversed wiring has been auto-detected/compensated in software since V105); the message now accurately describes what actually happened (a commutation/current-response check, not a wiring-direction problem).

**Assets**
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V106.bin` — application firmware image (flash at 0x08003000, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

**Integrity**
- SHA-256: `edb06ca112a7d24b0581e0b157a4524928067a46f8dc850ce22df8128092a758`
- Size: 94908 bytes

Built from commit `e1f8611` on `Bootloader_main`.

## V105 (2026-07-05)

Spectral BLDC firmware **V105** — reversed-wiring auto-calibration

`#Cal` now auto-detects reversed motor phase wiring during the open-loop spin and compensates it in software as a phase B<->C reflection, instead of failing and telling you to physically swap phases. Angle-offset calibration is now found automatically as part of `#Cal` itself (deterministic rotor-lock + verify + symmetry-sweep), so the standalone `#Calangle` command has been removed. `#Info` now reports the true firmware version instead of a stale EEPROM value. Existing calibrated units are unaffected and do not need `#Default`.

**Assets**
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V105.bin` — application firmware image (flash at 0x08003000, target STM32F103CB).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256 for download verification by the web flasher.

**Integrity**
- SHA-256: `0bd80ea038b8497fca8ab6a613b083d28e3473b360fa152b512b8ab0304dedb5`
- Size: 91732 bytes

Built from commit `b7dded3` on `Bootloader_main`. Includes reversed-wiring auto-calibration (`commutation_dir` detection + phase B<->C reflection) and deterministic rotor-lock angle-offset calibration.

## V104 (2026-06-19)

Spectral BLDC firmware **V104** — bootloader build.

#### Assets
- `spectral-bldc-firmware-V104.bin` — firmware image (90,968 bytes).
- `firmware.json` — manifest with version, size, and SHA-256.

#### Integrity
- SHA-256: `76d70a6091218d74021eeef55c31d39f19fe97f68e2b236169f84c708518a360`
- Size: 90968 bytes

Built from commit 20765c9 on `Bootloader_main`. Includes CAN Vlim command and bootloader support.

## v101 (2025-09-29)

Some small fixes added based on STEPFOC code that is a clone of this code.

2. Fixed some issues related to gripper mode where it vibrates

NOTE added another entry to EEPROM memory. Loading this code to update your previous code you will need to run #Default to 
load that new entry in EEPROM!

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/appendix/compatibility/ -->

# Versions and compatibility

Which Spectral firmware release works with which bootloader, gripper hardware, Python library and ROS 2 driver.
One row per firmware release, newest first; the last column names the version of this site, a gripper release, that
describes it.

| Firmware (Spectral) | Released | Bootloader | SSG-48 gripper | Python library (Spectral-BLDC) | ROS 2 driver | Docs (gripper release) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 110 | 2026-11-13 | required | V2, V1.1 | 1.22 or newer (names for parameters 90 to 93; 1.21 reads them by their numbers) | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2, msg_gripper_ros2 | 2 |
| 109 | 2026-11-10 | required | V2, V1.1 | 1.21 or newer (1.20 swaps object detection 1 and 2) | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2, msg_gripper_ros2 | 2 |
| 107 | 2026-08-26 | required (installed on grippers shipped with 105 or newer) | V2, V1.1 | 1.20 or newer | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2, msg_gripper_ros2 | 2 |
| 106 | 2026-07-06 | required | V1.1 | 1.19 or newer | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2 | not published |
| 105 | 2026-07-05 | required | V1.1 | 1.19 or newer | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2 | not published |
| 104 | 2026-06-19 | required (the first release built for the bootloader, from Bootloader_main) | V1.1 | 1.19 or newer | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2 | the Spectral Micro site, version 101 |
| 101 | 2025-09-29 | none (flashed with a programming adapter) | V1.1 | 1.17 or newer | ssg48_adaptive_electric_gripper_ros2 | the Spectral Micro site, version 101 |

Send_Respond_Device_Info returns the firmware release a gripper runs; `#Info` prints it over UART.

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/terminology/ -->

# Glossary

**Action bit**
:   A bit of the move command: 1 carries out the move, 0 leaves the gripper idle with the command stored. The
    action status of the answer repeats this bit.

**Activated**
:   A flag the gripper keeps, set by the activate bit of the move command or by `#Gripact`. A move is carried out
    only while the gripper is activated and calibrated.

**CAN ID** (node ID)
:   The address of the gripper on the CAN bus, 0 to 13; every gripper ships as 0. It occupies bits 10 to 7 of the
    11-bit CAN frame identifier; the command ID occupies bits 6 to 1 and the error bit is bit 0.

**CANvas**
:   Source Robotics' USB-to-CAN adapter. It appears as a serial port and speaks slcan, which `python-can`, Motor
    GUI and the ROS 2 drivers use.

**Coupler connector**
:   The round part on the back of the body that mounts the gripper: one for PAROL6, one for PAR6, a UR5 adapter
    plate, and a template for your own flange.

**Current limit** (grip force)
:   The current, in mA, the driver may put into the motor during a move. Torque is current times the motor's
    torque constant. It limits grip force; the conversion to newtons depends on the motor and mechanism. See
    [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) for the ideal model and measurement limits.

**Driver**
:   The Spectral Micro board inside the body: field-oriented control of the motor, the gripper state machine and
    the CAN and UART interfaces. The gripper's firmware is the driver's firmware.

**E-stop bit**
:   A bit of the move command. 1 stops the gripper and raises the gripper E-stop error, which comes back at every
    cycle while the last command's bit is 1: send a command with the bit at 0, then clear the error.

**Error bit**
:   Bit 0 of every CAN frame identifier the driver sends: 1 while any error is active.

**Field-oriented control** (FOC)
:   Controlling the motor's current as a vector relative to the rotor, from the driver's encoder. It gives a
    brushless motor a known, limited torque at standstill, which is what makes a force-controlled gripper out of
    it.

**Fin-ray finger**
:   A finger whose two flexible sides are joined by ribs, so that it bends around an object pressed into it. The
    repository has printable ones for the jaw plates.

**Firmware release**
:   One build of the Spectral firmware, numbered 101, 104, 105, … and tagged `v101`, `V104`, `V105`, … in the
    driver's repository. `#Info` prints the release a gripper runs. This documentation describes one release; the
    version selector switches between them.

**Gripper calibration**
:   The routine (`Send_gripper_calibrate`, `#Gripcal`) that opens the jaws fully, then closes them fully, at low
    force, finds both end stops and sets positions 0 and 255 just inside them. Needed after every power-up.

**Gripper mode**
:   The driver's mode in which it runs a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved): move commands with a jaw position, a speed
    and a current limit, and object detection.

**Motor calibration**
:   The driver's own calibration of the motor (`#Cal`): the resistance and inductance measured, the pole pairs
    found, the encoder aligned, the motor constants measured. Done once, at the factory or when you build the
    gripper; not to be confused with the gripper calibration.

**Object detection**
:   The gripper's report of why the jaws stopped: 0 still moving, 1 an object stopped them while closing, 2 an
    object stopped them while opening, 3 they reached the commanded position.

**Position**
:   The jaw position as the gripper commands and reports it: 0 fully open, 255 fully closed, linear in between.

**Rack and pinion**
:   The gripper's mechanism: a pinion on the motor meshes with two racks that run on the linear rail in opposite
    directions, so one motor moves both jaws symmetrically.

**Speed**
:   The speed of a move, 0 to 255, mapped by the firmware to 40 to 80000 encoder ticks per second of the motor.

**Stroke**
:   How much the distance between the jaw plates changes from fully open to fully closed: 48 mm. Each jaw
    travels half of it.

**Timeout error** (watchdog)
:   The driver's CAN watchdog, as the gripper reports it: when the watchdog is set (`Send_Watchdog`) and no
    gripper command or status request arrives in time, the gripper stops and raises it.

**Watchdog**
:   A timer the driver resets with every gripper command (full or empty) and every status request it receives.
    When it is set and runs out, the gripper reports a timeout error and stops.

# API reference

The gripper's CAN messages and UART commands, its status and error bits, and the Python library calls that send
them, for the firmware named on the landing page. The gripper is a Spectral Micro BLDC driver in gripper mode and accepts the
driver's whole command set; only what a gripper host or a self-built gripper needs is here, the rest is in the
[Spectral reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/).

- [CAN messages](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/): the identifier, and the gripper, system and status messages
- [UART commands](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/): the gripper commands, the driver setup commands, status and utility
- [Errors and status bits](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/errors/)
- [Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/python/): which library call sends which message

**Conventions.** Bytes are numbered from 0 and multi-byte values are big-endian. Bits are numbered from the most
significant: bit 7 is the first flag in a byte. The position is 0 (open) to 255 (closed), the speed 0 to 255, the
current in mA. UART command names are case-sensitive.

The command IDs, frame lengths and responses are read from the firmware's source at its release tag when the site
is built, so they cannot drift from the firmware; the descriptions and byte layouts are written by hand.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can-tools/ -->

# CAN frame tool and downloads

Build or inspect a frame using the command definitions of this manual's firmware release. All calculations
run in your browser; the tool does not connect to an adapter or send commands to hardware.

## Downloads

[Command definitions (JSON)](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/can/protocol-V110.json) · [Gripper DBC](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/assets/can/protocol-V110-gripper.dbc)

The JSON includes the firmware tag, source commit, message IDs, every documented layout and its bit order.
The DBC files cover **nodes 0 to 13**, with both the clean and fault-bit identifiers of driver replies.
Reserved commands are omitted. Values use the firmware's native units: ticks, ticks/s, mA and the units in
the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/).

An RTR request uses the same identifier as its data reply. DBC describes the **data reply**; it does not
represent the request's RTR flag or the empty gripper status poll. Both are supported by the browser tool.

The gripper's two object-detection bits have an unusual order: bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit.
The DBC signal `gripper_object_detection_raw` retains the wire value and supplies text labels (raw 2 =
object while closing, raw 1 = object while opening). The browser decoder converts that pair to the firmware's
numeric status (1 = closing, 2 = opening).

## Try a frame

The example `0x07A`, data `C8 1E 01 2C C0`, is a command to gripper node 0: position 200, speed 30,
current 300 mA, activate and action set, E-stop and release direction clear. These are an illustration of the
encoding; the device's current and motion limits still apply. Select another message above the fields to build
one of its documented forms. To inspect a reply, enter its identifier and data bytes below.

<div class="can-tool" data-schema="../../assets/can/protocol-V110.json" markdown="0">
  <p class="can-tool__status" role="status">Loading the firmware's command definitions…</p>
  <fieldset><legend>Build a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-node">Node ID (0–13)</label><input id="ct-node" name="node" type="number" min="0" max="13" step="1" value="0">
    <label for="ct-command">Message and layout</label><select id="ct-command" name="command"></select>
    <label><input name="error" type="checkbox"> Driver reply has an active fault (error bit 1)</label>
    <div class="can-tool__fields"></div>
    <button type="button" name="build" class="md-button md-button--primary">Build frame</button>
    <pre class="can-tool__built" aria-live="polite"></pre>
    <button type="button" name="use" class="md-button">Use this frame in the decoder</button>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset><legend>Decode a frame</legend>
    <label for="ct-id">CAN identifier (hex)</label><input id="ct-id" name="identifier" type="text" value="0x07A" spellcheck="false">
    <label for="ct-data">Data bytes (hex, up to eight)</label><input id="ct-data" name="data" type="text" value="C8 1E 01 2C C0" spellcheck="false">
    <label><input name="remote" type="checkbox"> Remote request (RTR; no payload)</label>
    <button type="button" name="decode" class="md-button md-button--primary">Decode frame</button>
    <div class="can-tool__decoded" aria-live="polite"></div>
  </fieldset>
  <noscript>Enable JavaScript for the frame tool, or use the reference tables and downloads above.</noscript>
</div>

**Check:** the example decodes to the values above. Change the identifier to `0x1FA` to see the same command
addressed to node 3. An invalid length or out-of-range field produces an explanation instead of a frame.

For wiring, termination, host timing and recovery, use [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/). To look up a
message's purpose and accepted lengths, use the [CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/).


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/ -->

# CAN messages

CAN 2.0, 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit identifiers. The identifier carries the node ID (bits 10 to 7, 0 to 13), the command ID
(bits 6 to 1, 0 to 63) and, in frames from the gripper, the error bit (bit 0). [Over CAN](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/can/)
explains how the pieces are used; this page lists them.

Three kinds of message:

- **Send_…** — the host sends data to the gripper. The gripper command is answered with Respond_Gripper_data_pack;
  the others are not answered.
- **Send_Respond_…** — the host asks for data with a **remote frame** (RTR bit set, no data) under the command ID;
  the gripper answers with a data frame under the same command ID.
- **Respond_…** — frames only the gripper sends.

Multi-byte values are big-endian (data[0] first); bits inside a byte are numbered from the most significant bit
(bit 7 first).

## The messages a gripper needs

| ID | Message | Direction | Length | Group |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | [Send_ESTOP](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_estop) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 1 | [Send_Clear_Error](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 9 | [Respond_Heartbeat](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#respond_heartbeat) | driver → host | 0 | Status requests |
| 10 | [Send_Respond_Ping](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_ping) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 0 | Status requests |
| 11 | [Send_CAN_ID](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_can_id) | host → driver | 1 | System |
| 12 | [Send_Idle](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 13 | [Send_Save_config](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 14 | [Send_Reset](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_reset) | host → driver | 0 | System |
| 15 | [Send_Watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) | host → driver | 5 | System |
| 23 | [Send_Respond_Temperature](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 24 | [Send_Respond_Voltage](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_voltage) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 25 | [Send_Respond_Device_Info](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_device_info) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 7 | Status requests |
| 26 | [Send_Respond_State_of_Errors](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors) | host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame | 0 (remote) / 2 | Status requests |
| 30 | [Send_Heartbeat_Setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) | host → driver | 4 | System |
| 60 | [Respond_Gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#respond_gripper_data_pack) | driver → host | 4 | Gripper |
| 61 | [Send_gripper_data_pack](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) | host → driver | 0, 5 | Gripper |
| 62 | [Send_gripper_calibrate](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) | host → driver | 0 | Gripper |

The driver's other messages (the motion commands, the gains and limits, the encoder and current requests) are
not listed here; they are in the [Spectral CAN reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/can/).

## By group

- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/): the move command and its answer, the gripper calibration
- [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/): node ID, E-stop, idle, save, reset, clear, watchdog, heartbeat setup
- [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/): temperature, voltage, identity, the driver's error flags, the heartbeat

## The Python library

Every message the host can send has a method of the same name in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, listed in
[Python library](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/python/).

## Tools and downloads

[Build or decode a CAN frame, and download this firmware's JSON and DBC definitions](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can-tools/).

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

The move command, its answer, and the gripper calibration. [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
explains what the gripper does with them.

### Send_gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 61</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 or 5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_data_pack()`</span></div>

The gripper command, for a driver set up as a gripper (`#Gripper 1`, saved). Position, speed and the current limit of the move, plus the activate, action and E-stop bits. A move is carried out only while the gripper is calibrated, activated and the action bit is 1. An empty frame (0 bytes) only asks for the state. The answer is sent before the driver acts on the frame, so it carries the state from before it. While the gripper calibration runs, send only the empty frame: a full one ends the calibration.

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | Position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1 |  | Speed | unsigned 8-bit | 0 slowest, 255 fastest |
| 2-3 |  | Current | signed 16-bit | current limit of the move in mA, the grip force; clamped by the firmware only at 2800 mA, see Force and speed for the safe range |
| 4 | 7 | Activate | bit | 1 activate the gripper, 0 deactivate |
| 4 | 6 | Action | bit | 1 go to the position, 0 idle |
| 4 | 5 | E-stop | bit | 1 raises the gripper E-stop error, again at every cycle while the last command's bit is 1 |
| 4 | 4 | Release direction | bit | read by the firmware but not used |

The driver answers with **Respond_Gripper_data_pack**.

---

### Respond_Gripper_data_pack

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 60</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span></div>

The driver's answer to Send_gripper_data_pack: position, measured current, and the state bits. Python attributes `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated`.

**The frame** (4 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | gripper_position | unsigned 8-bit | 0 fully open, 255 fully closed |
| 1-2 |  | gripper_current | signed 16-bit | measured current in mA |
| 3 | 7 | gripper_activated | bit | 1 activated |
| 3 | 6 | gripper_action_status | bit | the action bit of the last command, as received; stays 1 while holding, not changed by the calibration |
| 3 | 5-4 | gripper_object_detection | 2 bits | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object detected while closing, 2 object detected while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | 3 | gripper_temperature_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 2 | gripper_timeout_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 1 | gripper_estop_error | bit |  |
| 3 | 0 | gripper_calibrated | bit | 1 calibrated |

---

### Send_gripper_calibrate

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 62</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_gripper_calibrate()`</span></div>

Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Needed after every power-up. It has no answer: poll with empty Send_gripper_data_pack frames until the calibrated bit is 1, and send nothing else meanwhile, since a full gripper command or Send_Clear_Error ends the calibration. With an error active the request is dropped: clear first. Each end is read under a light 100 mA push; position 0 is set 32 encoder ticks inside the open stop and 255 16 ticks from the closed one. Ends less than 1000 ticks apart leave the gripper uncalibrated. A new request starts the routine from the beginning. The driver's current limit (parameter 16) is not touched.

The driver does not answer this command.

---


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/ -->

# System

Node ID, stopping, saving, resetting, clearing errors, the watchdog and the heartbeat setup: the driver's system
messages a gripper host uses.

### Send_CAN_ID

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 11</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">1 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_CAN_ID()`</span></div>

Gives the driver a new node ID, 0 to 13 (the firmware accepts up to 15, but the bootloader reserves 14 and 15: a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN). The driver answers to the new ID at once; Send_Save_config keeps it over a power cycle and also writes it into the bootloader's board ID.

**1 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | ID | unsigned 8-bit | 0 to 15 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_ESTOP

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 0</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_ESTOP()`</span></div>

Stops the motor and raises the E-stop error, which stays until Send_Clear_Error. A running calibration ends. From firmware 110 `#Estop` does the same over UART.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Idle

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 12</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Idle()`</span></div>

Puts the driver in idle mode (the motor coasts or brakes, see Send_Settings).

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Save_config

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 13</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Save_config()`</span></div>

Writes the current configuration (gains, limits, the motor calibration, CAN ID, heartbeat, watchdog, gripper flag, and from firmware 110 brake or coast) to the EEPROM. The gripper calibration is not saved: it runs after every power-up.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Reset

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 14</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Reset()`</span></div>

Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again; this is how a firmware update begins.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Clear_Error

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 1</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Clear_Error()`</span></div>

Clears the error flags and goes to idle. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back; the gripper's E-stop error comes back while the last gripper command's E-stop bit is 1, so send a command with the bit at 0 first. A clear also ends a running gripper calibration. A calibration error is cleared only by calibrating.

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Watchdog

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 15</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">5 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Watchdog()`</span></div>

Sets the watchdog: the gripper command (full or empty) and the status requests reset it, Send_Clear_Error, Send_gripper_calibrate and the setup messages do not; when the time runs out the driver reports a watchdog error and does what the action byte says. 0 turns it off (the default). Hold and descend run for the fallback time, then the after-action (parameters 2 and 5), and only when the watchdog runs out while the driver is in gripper mode. From firmware 110 a watchdog that runs out while the driver is idle starts neither, also not when the next gripper command arrives. The Spectral Micro site explains each action, [The watchdog](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/06-operation/watchdog/).

**5 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Time | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |
| 4 |  | Action | unsigned 8-bit | 0 legacy (the motor disabled, coasting), 1 hold the position, 2 brake (not current-limited), 3 coast, 4 descend at the fallback current and speed; other values act as 0 |

The driver does not answer this command.

---

### Send_Heartbeat_Setup

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 30</span><span class="fact">host → driver</span><span class="fact">4 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()`</span></div>

Sets the heartbeat interval in ms; 0 turns the heartbeat off (the default). Kept by Send_Save_config.

**4 bytes**

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-3 |  | Interval | unsigned 32-bit | ms; 0 = off |

---

## Parameters a gripper uses

Settings without a message of their own are numbered parameters. Send_Parameter (ID 36) writes one,
Send_Get_Parameter (ID 37) asks for one, and the driver answers with Respond_Parameter (ID 38). The frames and the
whole list are on the Spectral Micro site,
[Parameters](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/can/parameters/). These concern a
gripper:

| Parameter | What it is | Values |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | the driver's current limit in mA, for the motor modes; gripper moves and the gripper calibration leave it as it is | a float |
| 18 | brake or coast when idle; kept by Send_Save_config | 1 brake, 0 coast; a driver that never saved it coasts |
| 90 | `#Rstint`: zero the velocity and current integrators on every setpoint command | 0 or 1; 0 on a gripper |
| 91 | `#Term`: the thermistor measurement | 0 or 1; 1 on a gripper |
| 92 | `#Gripper`: gripper mode, in force at once; written only while the driver is idle | 0 or 1; 1 on a gripper |
| 93 | read only: the gripper's stroke between positions 0 and 255, in encoder ticks | 0 until the gripper is calibrated |

Parameters 90 to 93 are new in firmware 110, and from 110 Send_Save_config keeps 18 too; it keeps 90 to 92 like
the other settings. A value outside the range is refused, and the value in force stays.

The Python library names them from 1.22 (`PARAM_RSTINT`, `PARAM_THERMISTOR`, `PARAM_GRIPPER_MODE`,
`PARAM_GRIPPER_STROKE`); 1.21 takes the numbers. `gripper.Send_Parameter(92, 1)` writes one;
`gripper.Send_Get_Parameter(93)` asks for one, and its answer, passed through `UnpackData`, lands in
`gripper.parameters[93]`.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/ -->

# Status requests

Remote frames the host sends under a command ID, answered by the gripper with a data frame under the same ID,
and the heartbeat the gripper sends on its own when it is set up.

### Send_Respond_Ping

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 10</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Ping()`</span></div>

Asks the driver to answer with an empty frame, to see that it is on the bus.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Ping**.

---

### Send_Respond_Temperature

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 23</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Temperature()`</span></div>

Asks for the thermistor temperature. Meaningful only with the thermistor enabled (`#Term 1`).

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | temperature | signed 16-bit | °C |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Temperature**.

---

### Send_Respond_Voltage

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 24</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Voltage()`</span></div>

Asks for the supply voltage.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-1 |  | voltage | unsigned 16-bit | mV |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Voltage**.

---

### Send_Respond_Device_Info

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 25</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_Device_Info()`</span></div>

Asks for the driver's identity: hardware version, batch date and serial number from the EEPROM, and the firmware release (from firmware 105 on this is the build's own version; before, a value from the EEPROM).

**The frame** (7 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 |  | HARDWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | PCB revision |
| 1 |  | BATCH_DATE | unsigned 8-bit | production batch |
| 2 |  | SOFTWARE_VERSION | unsigned 8-bit | firmware release, e.g. 107 |
| 3-6 |  | SERIAL_NUMBER | unsigned 32-bit | serial number |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_Device_Info**.

---

### Send_Respond_State_of_Errors

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 26</span><span class="fact">host → driver as a remote frame, driver → host as a data frame</span><span class="fact">remote frame, 0 bytes</span><span class="fact">Python: `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()`</span></div>

Asks for every error flag and the calibrated, activated and watchdog states.

**The frame** (2 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 7 | error | bit | any error is active |
| 0 | 6 | temperature_error | bit | motor over the temperature limit |
| 0 | 5 | encoder_error | bit | magnet not detected or misaligned |
| 0 | 4 | vbus_error | bit | supply voltage outside the limits |
| 0 | 3 | driver_error | bit | the MOSFET driver reports undervoltage, thermal shutdown or overcurrent |
| 0 | 2 | velocity_error | bit | speed over the limit |
| 0 | 1 | current_error | bit | reserved; never set by this firmware |
| 0 | 0 | estop_error | bit | Send_ESTOP was received |
| 1 | 7 | calibrated | bit | the motor is calibrated |
| 1 | 6 | activated | bit | the controller is activated |
| 1 | 5 | watchdog_error | bit | the watchdog ran out |

The driver answers with **Send_Respond_State_of_Errors**.

---

### Respond_Heartbeat

<div class="cmd-facts" markdown><span class="fact">ID 9</span><span class="fact">driver → host</span><span class="fact">0 bytes</span></div>

The frame the driver sends on its own at the heartbeat interval (Send_Heartbeat_Setup); empty. Off by default. Any other frame the driver sends resets the heartbeat timer, so a driver that answers motion commands at a high rate never sends a heartbeat.

**The frame** (0 bytes)

| Byte | Bit | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|

---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/ -->

# UART commands

The commands a gripper needs over the driver's serial port, for the firmware release this site describes. The
kind, the argument type, the mode a command enters and what it prints are read from the firmware; the
descriptions are written by hand. [Over UART](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/uart/) says where the port is and how it is
used.

## Syntax

```
#<Name> [number]
```

- A **Set/Get** command sets the value when a number follows and prints the current value either way.
- A **Get** command only prints.
- An **Action** command does something; a number after it is ignored.
- Names are case-sensitive, at most 19 characters; the number at most 19; the line ends with LF (CR before it is
  fine). 256000 baud, 8N1, 3.3 V.
- A name the parser does not know is answered `Unknown command`.

## The commands a gripper needs

| Command | Kind | Argument | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`#Cal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Calibrated`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#CANID`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Cbw`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Clear`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Default`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Error`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Estop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Gripact`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcal`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Action |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripcur`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripinfo`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Get |  | Gripper |
| [`#Gripper`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Grippos`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripstop`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Gripvel`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/) | Set/Get | int | Gripper |
| [`#Help`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Ilim`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |
| [`#Info`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Kiiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Kpiq`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Kt`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get |  | Driver setup |
| [`#LED`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Set/Get | int | Status and utility |
| [`#Magnet`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Mode`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Reset`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Action |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Save`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Action |  | Driver setup |
| [`#Temp`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |
| [`#Term`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/) | Set/Get | int | Driver setup |

| [`#Vbus`](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/) | Get |  | Status and utility |

The driver's other commands (motion, gains, the calibration settings) are in the
[Spectral UART reference](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/reference/uart/).

## By group

- [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/): gripper mode, the gripper calibration, the setpoints, the state
- [Driver setup](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/): the defaults, the motor parameters and calibration, the gains, the thermistor, the node ID, saving
- [Status and utility](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/): identity, errors, temperature, help
