<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/gripper/ -->

# Gripper

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Gripper` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Whether this driver is a gripper. A gripper has it set and saved; `#Default` clears it, so set it again after restoring the defaults. | the flag |
| `#Gripcal` | Action |  | Starts the gripper calibration (the jaws find their end stops). Clear any error first; until `#Gripinfo` reports it calibrated, send no `#Grippos` or `#Clear`, which end it. Enters **gripper calibration** mode. | `Gripper calibration!` |
| `#Gripinfo` | Get |  | Prints the gripper state: gripper mode, calibrated, activated, the position, speed and current setpoints, the E-stop and action bits, the object detection, and the end stops in encoder ticks. | the report |
| `#Gripstop` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The gripper E-stop bit. While it is 1, the E-stop error is raised again at every cycle: set it to 0 before `#Clear`. | the bit |
| `#Gripact` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The activate bit. | the bit |
| `#Gripcur` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The current limit of gripper moves | the setpoint |
| `#Gripvel` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 255 | The speed setpoint of gripper moves. | the setpoint |
| `#Grippos` | Set/Get | int: 0 (open) to 255 (closed) | The position setpoint; also activates the gripper, sets the action bit and goes to gripper mode. Enters **gripper** mode. | the current position |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/setup/ -->

# Driver setup

The driver commands a self-built gripper is configured with; [Driver configuration](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/first-run/)
is the procedure.

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Kpiq` | Set/Get | gain | Kp of the Iq current loop; also sets Kpid. | the current value |
| `#Kiiq` | Set/Get | gain | Ki of the Iq current loop; also sets Kiid. | the current value |
| `#Kt` | Set/Get | Nm/A | The torque constant, found by calibration. | the current value |
| `#Cal` | Get |  | Runs the calibration routine (see Calibration): it measures R and L, finds the pole pairs, the phase order and the angle offset, and measures Kt, KV and the flux linkage. | the calibration log |
| `#Cal` | Get |  | Runs the calibration routine (see Calibration): it measures R and L, finds the pole pairs, the phase order and the angle offset, and measures Kt, KV and the flux linkage. | the calibration log |
| `#Save` | Action |  | Writes the configuration to the EEPROM. Do it after calibration and after tuning. | `Save` |
| `#Ilim` | Set/Get | int: current in mA | The driver's Iq current limit outside gripper mode; the firmware clamps it to 2800 mA. Gripper moves use Gripcur instead and leave this limit as it is. | the current limit |
| `#Tlim` | Set/Get | int: temperature in °C | The temperature at which the temperature error is raised; 75 by default. | `Temp limit N` |
| `#Default` | Action |  | Writes the factory defaults to the EEPROM, including the serial number, hardware version and batch date, and clears the gripper flag, heartbeat and watchdog. Back those up first. | `Loaded default config!` |
| `#Term` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Enables the thermistor measurement and the temperature error (off by default). | the setting |
| `#Cbw` | Set/Get | bandwidth in Hz | The current loop bandwidth calibration uses to compute Kpiq and Kiiq. | the bandwidth |
| `#CANID` | Set/Get | int: 0 to 13 | The CAN node ID. Use 0 to 13: the firmware accepts 14 and 15, but the bootloader reserves them and a driver on one of those cannot be updated over CAN. Save keeps it over a power cycle and also writes it into the bootloader's board ID. | the ID, or `Invalid CAN ID` |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/uart/utility/ -->

# Status and utility

| Command | Kind | Argument | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#Estop` | Action |  | The driver's E-stop, as Send_ESTOP over CAN: the motor is released, a running calibration (the motor's or the gripper's) ends, and the E-stop error stays until `#Clear`. It shows in `#Error` and in Send_Respond_State_of_Errors, not in the gripper's own E-stop bit. New in firmware 110. | `E-stop` |
| `#Magnet` | Get |  | Reads the encoder's magnet status. | `Magnet Good` or `Magnet Bad` |
| `#Reset` | Action |  | Resets the driver. From firmware 105 the reset lands in the bootloader, which waits 2 s for a flashing host and then starts the firmware again. | nothing |
| `#Temp` | Get |  | Prints the thermistor temperature. | °C, or `Temp Off` while the thermistor is disabled |
| `#Mode` | Get |  | Prints the control mode. | `Idle mode`, `Position control`, `Speed control`, `Current control`, `PD control`, `Open loop`, `Gripper mode`, `Gripper calib mode` |
| `#Vbus` | Get |  | Prints the supply voltage. | mV |
| `#Error` | Get |  | Prints which errors are active. | `No errors!` or `In error state!` followed by one line per active error |
| `#Clear` | Action |  | Clears the errors and goes to idle, and ends a running gripper calibration. An error whose cause is still present comes straight back, the gripper's E-stop too while `#Gripstop` is 1; a calibration error is cleared only by calibrating (or `#Calibrated 1`). Enters **idle** mode. | `Clear errors` |
| `#Help` | Action |  | Prints a short command reference. Added in firmware 106. | the reference |
| `#Info` | Action |  | Prints the driver's identity and state: hardware version, batch date and firmware version, the ISR time, the CAN ID, the motor calibration, the thermistor and temperature, the supply voltage and the motor parameters (phase direction and order, pole pairs, R, L, Kt, KV). The serial number is printed by `#SERNUM`, the errors by `#Error`, gripper mode by `#Gripper`. | the report |
| `#Calibrated` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | The calibrated flag. `#Calibrated 1` clears a calibration error without calibrating; the motor may still be uncalibrated. | the flag |
| `#LED` | Set/Get | int: 0 or 1 | Turns the status LED on or off. | the LED state |


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/errors/ -->

# Errors and status bits

## The gripper's state byte

Byte 3 of Respond_Gripper_data_pack, the answer to every gripper command, bits numbered from the most significant:

| Bit | Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 7 | `activated` | the activate flag is set |
| 6 | `action_status` | the action bit of the last gripper command, as received (`#Grippos` sets it to 1); it stays 1 while the gripper holds, and the calibration does not change it. The state of a move is in `object_detection` |
| 5, 4 | `object_detection` | bit 5 is the low bit, bit 4 the high bit: 0 moving, 1 object found while closing, 2 object found while opening, 3 at the position |
| 3 | `temperature_error` | the thermistor in the windings is above the limit |
| 2 | `timeout_error` | the driver's CAN watchdog ran out |
| 1 | `estop_error` | the E-stop bit of a command was received |
| 0 | `calibrated` | the gripper calibration is done |

The Python library's attributes are `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`,
`gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error` and `gripper_calibrated`; library
1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with its two bits swapped (1 and 2 exchanged), 1.21 and newer
read them right.

## The driver's error flags

The flags as the firmware keeps them, the line `#Error` prints for each, and where each sits in the two bytes of
Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (bits numbered from the most significant).

| Flag | `#Error` prints | Byte, bit | Raised when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Error` | `In error state!` | 0, 7 | any of the flags below is set (also the error bit of every CAN identifier) |
| `temperature_error` | `Temp error` | 0, 6 | the thermistor reads above `#Tlim` (75 °C) |
| `encoder_error` | `Encoder error` | 0, 5 | the driver's encoder does not see its magnet |
| `Vbus_error` | `Vbus error` | 0, 4 | the supply is below 9 V or above `#Vmax` (29 V after `#Default`) |
| `Driver_error` | `Driver error (undervoltage, thermal shutdown, or overcurrent)` | 0, 3 | the driver stage's fault output is active |
| `Velocity_error` | `Velocity error` | 0, 2 | the motor speed exceeds the driver's limit |
| `Current_error` | `Current error` | 0, 1 | never in this firmware; reserved |
| `ESTOP_error` | `Received ESTOP command` | 0, 0 | Send_ESTOP was received |
| `Calibrated` (0) | `Not calibrated` | 1, 7 (1 = calibrated) | the driver's motor calibration is missing |
| `Activated` | — | 1, 6 | the activated flag, not an error |
| `Watchdog_error` | `Watchdog error` | 1, 5 | the watchdog time passed without a valid CAN frame |

The gripper's `timeout_error` is the driver's `Watchdog_error`; the gripper's `temperature_error` is the driver's.
The gripper's `estop_error` is its own, raised by the E-stop bit of the gripper command, and is distinct from the
driver's `ESTOP_error` raised by Send_ESTOP.

## Clearing

Send_Clear_Error and `#Clear` clear every flag, the gripper's E-stop included, and go to idle; a flag whose cause
persists is set again at once. The gripper's `estop_error` is raised again at every cycle while the E-stop bit of
the last gripper command (or `#Gripstop`) is 1: send a gripper command with the bit at 0 first, then clear. The
driver's `Calibrated` flag is set only by the motor calibration (`#Cal`).

## The LED

The driver's status LED is inside the housing: three short flashes and a pause in normal operation, flashing
every 0.5 s during the motor calibration, on steadily in error mode or while the motor is not calibrated.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/python/ -->

# Python library

The `Spectral-BLDC` package ([Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python),
`pip install Spectral-BLDC`) has one method per CAN message in `Spectral_BLDC.SpectralCAN`, and
`Spectral_BLDC.CanCommunication` for the bus. [With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/) shows how they are used
with the gripper.

## Calls and messages

The calls for the messages this reference describes; the library has one for every message of the driver.

| Library call | Sends | Answered with | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Send_gripper_data_pack()` | Send_gripper_data_pack (ID 61) | Respond_Gripper_data_pack | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_data_pack) |
| `Send_gripper_calibrate()` | Send_gripper_calibrate (ID 62) | — | [Gripper](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/gripper/#send_gripper_calibrate) |
| `Send_CAN_ID()` | Send_CAN_ID (ID 11) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_can_id) |
| `Send_ESTOP()` | Send_ESTOP (ID 0) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_estop) |
| `Send_Idle()` | Send_Idle (ID 12) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_idle) |
| `Send_Save_config()` | Send_Save_config (ID 13) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_save_config) |
| `Send_Reset()` | Send_Reset (ID 14) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_reset) |
| `Send_Clear_Error()` | Send_Clear_Error (ID 1) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_clear_error) |
| `Send_Watchdog()` | Send_Watchdog (ID 15) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_watchdog) |
| `Send_Heartbeat_Setup()` | Send_Heartbeat_Setup (ID 30) | — | [System](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/system/#send_heartbeat_setup) |
| `Send_Respond_Ping()` | Send_Respond_Ping (ID 10) | Send_Respond_Ping (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_ping) |
| `Send_Respond_Temperature()` | Send_Respond_Temperature (ID 23) | Send_Respond_Temperature (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_temperature) |
| `Send_Respond_Voltage()` | Send_Respond_Voltage (ID 24) | Send_Respond_Voltage (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_voltage) |
| `Send_Respond_Device_Info()` | Send_Respond_Device_Info (ID 25) | Send_Respond_Device_Info (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_device_info) |
| `Send_Respond_State_of_Errors()` | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (ID 26) | Send_Respond_State_of_Errors (data frame) | [Status requests](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/reference/can/status/#send_respond_state_of_errors) |

`Send_gripper_data_pack(position, speed, current, activate, action, estop, release_direction)` sends the 5-byte
move; called without arguments it sends the empty frame that only asks for the state.

## Receiving

`CanCommunication.receive_can_messages(timeout)` returns `(message, ids)`: the raw `python-can` message and a tuple
`ids` with `node_id`, `command_id` and `error_bit` from the identifier, or `(None, None)` after the timeout.
`SpectralCAN.UnpackData(message, ids)` decodes the message into the object's attributes:

| Message | Attributes |
|---|---|
| Respond_Gripper_data_pack | `gripper_position`, `gripper_current`, `gripper_activated`, `gripper_action_status`, `gripper_object_detection`, `gripper_temperature_error`, `gripper_timeout_error`, `gripper_estop_error`, `gripper_calibrated` |
| Send_Respond_State_of_Errors | `error`, `temperature_error`, `encoder_error`, `vbus_error`, `driver_error`, `velocity_error`, `current_error`, `estop_error`, `calibrated`, `activated`, `watchdog_error` |
| Send_Respond_Temperature | `temperature` |
| Send_Respond_Voltage | `voltage` |
| Send_Respond_Device_Info | `HARDWARE_VERSION`, `BATCH_DATE`, `SOFTWARE_VERSION`, `SERIAL_NUMBER` |

!!! note "Object detection in the library"
    Library 1.20 and older assemble `gripper_object_detection` with the two bits swapped relative to the
    firmware, so they report 1 where the gripper sends 2 (object detected while opening) and 2 where it sends 1
    (object detected while closing); 0 and 3 are unaffected. 1.21 and newer read them right.

# Guides

Worked examples around the gripper.

- [Basic control in Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/guides/basic-control/): the shortest program that calibrates the gripper and opens and
  closes it, from the product repository's README.
- [Teleoperation with two grippers](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/guides/teleoperation/): one gripper follows the other and pushes back what it
  feels, over one CAN bus and a few lines of Python.

Building a gripper yourself is in the manual, the [Build guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/build/). More examples,
for the driver as much as for the gripper, are in the
[Spectral-BLDC-Python examples](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples) and in
the [Spectral guides](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/guides/).

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/guides/basic-control/ -->

# Basic control in Python

The shortest program that drives the gripper: it connects through the CANvas adapter, clears the errors,
calibrates, then closes and opens every three seconds and prints what the gripper answers.

It is the example from
the product repository's README; `pip install Spectral-BLDC` is the only requirement. Change `COM20` to your
adapter's port (`/dev/ttyACM0` on Linux) and `node_id` to the gripper's CAN ID if you changed it from 0.

!!! danger
    700 mA closes the jaws with real force, about 38 N. Keep fingers out of the jaws, and start with a lower current
    if the gripper is new to you.

```python
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import time

Communication1 = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM20', bitrate=1000000)
Motor1 = Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=0, communication=Communication1)

Motor1.Send_Clear_Error()
Motor1.Send_gripper_calibrate()
time.sleep(4)

temp_var = 0
while True:
   if temp_var == 0:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(50,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 1
   elif temp_var == 1:
      Motor1.Send_gripper_data_pack(240,100,700,1,1,0,0)
      temp_var = 0

   message, UnpackedMessageID = Communication1.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.2)

   if message is not None:
      print(f"Message is: {message}")
      print(f"Node ID is : {UnpackedMessageID.node_id}")
      print(f"Message ID is: {UnpackedMessageID.command_id}")
      print(f"Error bit is: {UnpackedMessageID.error_bit}")
      print(f"Timestamp is: {message.timestamp}")

   time.sleep(3)
```

Each answer printed is the one to the command just sent, so it still shows the state from before that move.
The arguments of `Send_gripper_data_pack`, in order: the position (0 open, 255 closed), the speed (0 to 255), the
current limit in mA (the force), then the activate bit, the action bit, the E-stop bit and the release direction.

[With Python](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/python/) explains the library's calls, [How the gripper works](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/06-operation/how-it-works/)
the state the gripper answers with, and [Force and speed](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/03-technical-data/force-and-speed/) what the
current means in newtons.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/guides/teleoperation/ -->

# Teleoperation with two grippers

Two grippers on one CAN bus, coupled so that each follows the other: squeeze one by hand and the other closes;
when the other meets an object, the one in your hand pushes back with the force it feels. A hundred lines of
Python, and the basis of a teleoperation setup with force feedback.

This guide does not use the gripper mode. Both drivers run in **current (torque) mode**, the driver's own motion
command, and the PC closes a position loop between them at a fixed rate. The gripper mode's position, speed and
object detection are not involved; the drivers are plain torque sources here.

## What you need

- Two grippers, calibrated as motors (a bought gripper is), with different node IDs: 0 and 1 (`#CANID 1`,
  `#Save` on one of them over UART).
- Both on one bus with the CANvas adapter, 24 V on both, termination at the two ends.
- `pip install Spectral-BLDC SourceRoboticsToolbox`.

!!! warning
    In current mode the gripper has no end-stop knowledge and no object detection: it pushes with whatever current
    the loop commands. Set the driver's current limit to the motor's rating (`#Ilim`) on both grippers, start
    with low gains, and keep fingers out of the jaws.

## The idea

Each driver is commanded a current proportional to the difference between the two positions, plus a damping
term on the speed difference and a little damping of its own motion:

$$
I_0 = K_p\,(p_1 - p_0) + K_d\,(v_1 - v_0) - K_k\, v_0, \qquad
I_1 = K_p\,(p_0 - p_1) + K_d\,(v_0 - v_1) - K_k\, v_1
$$

$p$ is the jaw position of each gripper in the same units, $v$ its speed. When the two positions agree, both
currents are zero and the grippers rest.

Move one by hand and the difference drives the other after it; block
the other, and the difference drives the one in your hand back with the same current, which is the force you
feel. $K_p$ is the stiffness of the virtual spring between them, $K_d$ its damping.

The two drivers' encoders do not read the same number at the same jaw position, so each position is referred to
a reference reading taken once with both grippers in the same position; the Source Robotics Toolbox's `Joint`
does that bookkeeping and unwraps the encoder over its 16384-tick turns.

## The code

```python
import time
import numpy as np
import Spectral_BLDC as Spectral
import SourceRoboticsToolbox as Toolbox

INTERVAL_S = 0.002                 # the loop rate: 500 Hz
REFERENCE = [10440, 13555]         # each gripper's raw encoder reading with both jaws in the same position

Kp, Kd, Kk = 650, 0.0055, 0.0003   # stiffness, damping between the two, damping of each

bus = Spectral.CanCommunication(bustype='slcan', channel='COM123', bitrate=1000000)
motors = [Spectral.SpectralCAN(node_id=i, communication=bus) for i in (0, 1)]
joints = [Toolbox.Joint(encoder_resolution=14, master_position=REFERENCE[i], gear_ratio=1, offset=0, dir=0)
          for i in (0, 1)]

position = np.zeros(2)             # each gripper's position, referred to its reference
sector_known = [False, False]
current = [0, 0]

while True:
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for i in (0, 1):               # command the currents; each answer carries position and speed
        motors[i].Send_data_pack_1(Position=None, Speed=None, Current=int(current[i]))
    for _ in (0, 1):
        message, ids = bus.receive_can_messages(timeout=0.001)
        if ids is None:
            continue
        i = ids[0]
        motors[i].UnpackData(message, ids)
        if not sector_known[i]:
            joints[i].determine_sector(motors[i].position)
            sector_known[i] = True
        position[i] = joints[i].get_joint_position(motors[i].position)

    current[0] = Kp * (position[1] - position[0]) + Kd * (motors[1].speed - motors[0].speed) - Kk * motors[0].speed
    current[1] = Kp * (position[0] - position[1]) + Kd * (motors[0].speed - motors[1].speed) - Kk * motors[1].speed

    time.sleep(max(0.0, INTERVAL_S - (time.perf_counter() - t0)))
```

The reference readings: with both grippers powered and their jaws set by hand to the same opening, read each
driver's position as the loop receives it (print `motors[i].position` with both currents at 0) and put the two
numbers in `REFERENCE`.

## Tuning

Start with `Kp` at a tenth of the value above and raise it until the follower tracks the leader without lagging;
raise `Kd` if the pair oscillates.

The current the formula produces is in mA and is clamped by each driver's
`#Ilim`, so the motor's rating is the ceiling of the force feedback. A fixed loop rate matters: a loop that
runs at an uneven rate makes the damping terms noisy.

The full example, with a timer for a precise loop rate, is
[gripper_teleop_PC_calc.py](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/tree/main/examples/Advanced/SSG48%20gripper%20bilateral%20teleop)
in the Python library's examples, and the [bilateral teleoperation guide](https://docs.source-robotics.com/Spectral-BLDC-docs/latest/guides/bilateral-teleoperation/)
on the Spectral Micro site explains the control law with a joint instead of a gripper.

# Getting help

- **Questions and discussion**: the [Source Robotics Discord](https://discord.gg/prjUvjmGpZ).
- **A problem with the gripper's hardware or its files**: an issue in the
  [product repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/issues); see
  [Report a problem](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/report-a-problem/) for what to include.
- **A problem with the firmware**: an issue in the [driver's repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller/issues);
  with the Python library, in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/issues);
  with the ROS 2 driver, in [its repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/source_robotics_msg_gripper_ros2/issues).
- **A mistake on a page of this site**: every page ends with a link to edit it and one to report it; see
  [Contributing](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/contributing/).
- **Orders and hardware**: [source-robotics.com](https://source-robotics.com/).

Before you ask, [Troubleshooting](https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/09-troubleshooting/) goes through the common symptoms, and the gripper's
status tells most of what anyone will ask you for.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/report-a-problem/ -->

# Report a problem

Open an issue in the [product repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG-48-adaptive-electric-gripper/issues)
for the gripper and its files, in the [driver's repository](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-Micro-BLDC-controller/issues)
for the firmware, or in [Spectral-BLDC-Python](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/Spectral-BLDC-Python/issues)
for the Python library. Include:

1. **The gripper**: bought or self-built, the hardware version, the fingers.
2. **The firmware release** the gripper runs: Send_Respond_Device_Info, or `#Info` over UART, which also prints
   the driver's configuration; add what `#Error` prints.
3. **The gripper's status** when the problem happens: the state and error bits of Respond_Gripper_data_pack, or
   `#Gripinfo`.
4. **What you did and what happened**: the commands, in order, with their position, speed and current, and the
   answers.
5. **How it is connected**: the robot or the adapter, the cable, the termination; a photo helps more than a
   description.

For a problem with this documentation, the *Report it* link at the end of the page opens an issue in the
documentation repository with the page already named.


---

<!-- https://docs.source-robotics.com/SSG48-gripper-docs/2/support/contributing/ -->

# Contributing

This documentation lives in [Source-Robotics/SSG48-gripper-docs](https://github.com/Source-Robotics/SSG48-gripper-docs).
A small fix can be made from the browser: the *Edit it on GitHub* link at the end of every page opens the page's
source, and GitHub turns your change into a pull request. For anything larger, open an issue first.

## How the site is built

- The pages are Markdown, built with MkDocs and the Material theme; the repository's `README.md` says how to
  preview it locally.
- The site describes one release of the Spectral firmware, named in `versions.yml`. The command IDs, frame
  lengths, the UART command list and what each prints in the API reference are read from the firmware's source at
  that release's tag by `tools/sync_firmware.py`; do not edit those facts in the pages. The descriptions of the
  commands are in `docs/includes/can_commands.yml` and `uart_commands.yml`, which list only the commands a
  gripper needs.
- Every push runs a strict build (a broken link fails it) and the tool tests. A push to `main` publishes the
  site with [mike](https://github.com/jimporter/mike), under the gripper release named by `docs_version` in
  `versions.yml`.

## House rules

- Facts come from the firmware and the product repository. When a page and the firmware disagree, the firmware
  is right; fix the page, or report the firmware.
- Spell commands exactly as the firmware does, even where the spelling looks wrong.
- Write for someone who has the gripper in front of them and wants to do one thing: say what to do, in order,
  then why.
- Three kinds of boxes: a note, a notice (damage) and a danger (injury). Use them for those, not for emphasis.
- Images: under 2400 px on the long side, with a caption that says what the reader should see.
